docs.title: What is Travel Planner?
docs.text:
Travel Planner is an app that takes the hard work out of trip planning. You enter your destination, travel dates, budget, and what you enjoy doing — and a team of AI specialists immediately gets to work on your behalf.

Within 30 seconds you have:

  • flight options and price guidance
  • hotels broken down by neighbourhood and budget level
  • activities ranked by how well they match your interests
  • must-see landmarks and places with ratings and links
  • free walking tours, linked to the guide's own booking page
  • visa entry requirements for your passport
  • local emergency numbers, your country's embassy, and survival phrases
  • SIM card and eSIM options
  • currency and money tips
  • local transport advice
  • a packing list tailored to your destination and weather
  • a full day-by-day itinerary

Everything appears on screen as it's ready — you don't wait for a single slow loading screen.

docs.title: Plan your trip
docs.text:
Flights Typical airlines, route options, rough price ranges, and advice on when to book — whether to grab a deal now or hold off for a better price.

Hotels The best neighbourhoods to stay in (explained by what makes each one good for your type of trip), accommodation options from budget hostels to boutique hotels, and approximate prices per night.

Activities A list of things to do, automatically sorted so the activities that match your stated interests appear first. A food lover planning a Tokyo trip sees izakayas and ramen tours near the top, not the standard tourist checklist.

Places to See Landmark highlights — temples, museums, viewpoints, markets — with visitor ratings, how long to allow, and links to read more. Sourced from live Google data and summarised by AI.

Free Walking Tours Free and pay-what-you-wish walking tours at your destination, collected from public listings on GuruWalk, FreeTour.com, FreeWalkingTour.com and SANDEMANs NewEurope. AI picks the ones that suit your interests and says why; each card links to the original tour page to book.

Day-by-day Itinerary A logical schedule that fits your activities into mornings, afternoons, and evenings, keeps walking distances sensible, and links to your chosen accommodation area. View it as a timeline grid or read it as a day-by-day list, with weather shown for each day.

docs.title: Know before you go
docs.text:
Visa Requirements Entry rules specific to your passport nationality: whether you need a visa, how to apply, what documents to bring, processing times, and fees.

Safety & Emergency Card The information you hope you never need but are glad to have. Local emergency numbers (police, ambulance, fire, tourist police), your nearest international hospital, your country's embassy address and after-hours phone number, 10 phonetic survival phrases in the local language, and local laws that travellers sometimes accidentally break. Printable as a clean card.

Travel Confidence Score An instant snapshot of how straightforward the trip is — scored across five dimensions: visa ease, safety, how widely English is spoken, tourist infrastructure quality, and whether your budget is realistic for the destination. Green means easy, amber means plan ahead, red means do your homework.

Travel Tips Cultural etiquette (what's polite, what's rude), safety advice, health precautions, tipping norms, dress codes for religious sites, and practical local knowledge you won't find on the booking site.

Weather Day-by-day forecast for your exact travel dates (Open-Meteo for trips within 16 days, seasonal climate estimates beyond) — on multi-city trips, each stop is forecast only for the days you're actually there, grouped under a city header.

docs.title: Travel smart
docs.text:
SIM Cards & eSIMs Which local carrier to use, typical data plan options and prices, whether an eSIM works for your phone, and where to buy one (airport, convenience store, carrier shop).

Currency & Money The local currency, rough exchange rates, whether to exchange before you travel or at the destination, ATM availability and fees, how widely cards are accepted, and digital payment culture.

Getting Around Airport transfer options with price ranges, how to use the local public transport, ride-hailing app availability, taxi culture, and intercity travel if you're visiting multiple cities.

Layover Optimizer Long layover on the way? Get a "make the most of it" mini-plan — whether you can leave the airport, transit visa notes, and a realistic timed excursion.

Itinerary Health Check An adversarial AI review of the finished plan — it hunts for pacing problems, timing clashes, visa deadlines you'd miss, weather conflicts with outdoor days, and budget overruns, and reports them with severity levels.

Flight Price Advisor Based on historical pricing patterns for your specific route, this tells you whether current prices are above or below average, recommends whether to book now or wait, and shows a chart of how prices typically move in the weeks before departure.

Smart Packing List A personalised checklist built from your destination, travel dates, planned activities, and weather forecast. Items are grouped by category (documents, clothing, electronics, medications, activity gear) with essentials flagged. Tick off items as you pack and add your own — saved automatically to your plan.

docs.title: Multi-city journeys
docs.text: Multiple stops, one search Enter an ordered list of stops (Paris → Rome → Barcelona) and every section covers every city, each item tagged with a 📍 city chip. Days are split across cities automatically, flights are searched per leg (including the transatlantic bookends) with one pick per leg and a running total, and the itinerary visits your cities in exactly the order you entered them. See Multi-City Trips.

docs.title: Personalised to you
docs.text:
Taste Graph The app learns your travel style from what you actually select — non-stop flights, boutique hotels, food-first activities — and quietly ranks matching options higher on every future search. No forms; it's mined from your saved plans. See Personalization.

Serendipity dial & pace Slide between famous classics and hidden local gems; choose a relaxed, balanced, or packed daily pace.

docs.title: Discover where to go
docs.text: Surprise Me Not sure where to go? Enter your origin, budget, travel dates, and interests, and get five curated destination suggestions. Each card shows estimated trip cost, typical weather for your dates, visa status for your passport, approximate flight time, and the specific reasons this destination suits your interests. Click "Plan this trip" to immediately start planning with that destination pre-filled.

docs.title: Save and organise
docs.text:
My Plan A drawer that follows you through the app. Select the exact flights, hotel, activities, and other items you want. See a live cost total as you build. Name your plan ("The Rainy Tokyo Adventure"), save it, and reload it whenever you come back.

Chat A conversational AI travel advisor. Questions are answered instantly from the model's own expertise; describe a trip and the full planning pipeline streams structured results into the conversation, asks targeted clarifying questions when something's missing, and re-runs only the affected sections when you say "make it cheaper". See Chat Assistant.

Shareable trip card Every saved plan gets a public share page with the complete trip — flights per leg, hotel, full itinerary with your notes, and all picks — downloadable as a single full-page PNG. See Plans & Sharing.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The app uses a team of specialist AI agents — 13 run in parallel when you search, with two more (pricing advisor, packing list) starting as soon as their inputs are ready. As each one finishes, its results appear on your screen immediately — so you see flights within a few seconds, then hotels, then activities, and so on. You're never waiting for everything to load at once.

Some results (like visa rules and emergency numbers) come from carefully maintained lookup tables and appear instantly, before any AI call has even finished. The AI agents then enhance these with more detail.

Once activities and hotels are ready, a final agent synthesises everything into your day-by-day itinerary.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
The Travel Planner backend is a FastAPI application. All endpoints are under /api/. Interactive documentation (Swagger UI) is available at /docs on any running instance.

Live API: https://travel-planner-backend-2hrxgxqboa-ew.a.run.app Local API: http://localhost:8001

Authentication: Most endpoints require a JWT Bearer token from the login response:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

Rate limits: endpoints that call the AI agents are limited per caller — the signed-in user, or the client IP for anonymous requests — over a rolling 10-minute window. Every accepted request counts, including cached responses and requests later rejected as invalid (422) or unauthenticated (401); only requests answered with 429 do not.

Bucket Endpoints Default limit search POST /api/search, POST /api/search/sync 10 chat POST /api/chat 30 compare POST /api/compare/destination 30 discover POST /api/discover 10 light_ai POST /api/flights, /hotels, /activities (and their /filtered variants), /flights/fare-calendar, /visa, /sim, /tips, /getting-around, /forex, /itinerary, /events, /walking-tours, /layover, /stress-test 60

Each bucket is counted separately. Over the limit the API answers 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header (seconds) and:

{"detail": "Too many requests — please wait 42 seconds and try again."}

Limits are configurable (see Configuration). The counter is in-process, so each backend instance counts on its own.

docs.title: POST /api/search — SSE streaming
docs.text:
The core endpoint. Submits a trip search and streams results in real time via Server-Sent Events.

Auth required: Yes

Request body:

{
  "origin": "London",
  "destination": "Tokyo",
  "departure_date": "2026-06-01",
  "return_date": "2026-06-14",
  "nationality": "British",
  "interests": ["food", "history", "nature"],
  "budget_usd": 4000,
  "num_travelers": 1,
  "residence_permits": [],
  "existing_visas": []
}

Response: Content-Type: text/event-stream

Each event:

data: {"type": "<event_type>", "data": <object>, "source": "static"|"ai"}\n\n

The final event:

data: {"type": "done"}\n\n

Event types and phases:

Event type Phase Source Description confidence 0 static Travel confidence score (safety / visa / budget / infrastructure) visa 0 then 1 static → ai Visa requirements sim 0 then 1 static → ai SIM card options tips 0 then 1 static → ai Travel tips getting_around 0 then 1 static → ai Local transport emergency_card 0 then 1 static → ai Emergency numbers, embassy, phrases, local laws flights 1 ai Flights guidance weather 1 ai Forecast for travel dates hotels 1 ai Hotels by neighbourhood and budget tier activities 1 ai Activities, relevance-sorted places_to_see 1 ai Must-visit landmarks walking_tours 1 ai Free walking tours crawled from provider city pages events 1 ai What's On: festivals, concerts, exhibitions forex 1 ai Currency and payment tips pricing_advisor 1 (deferred) ai Flight price trend and booking recommendation packing_list 1 (deferred) ai Personalised packing checklist itinerary 2 ai Day-by-day schedule

Static-backed events (visa, sim, tips, getting_around, emergency_card): Phase 0 sends static data immediately. Phase 1 replaces it with AI-enriched data. If Phase 1 fails, the static data is retained — no error is shown for these sections.

Deferred events: pricing_advisor triggers when ≥ 3 flight prices are available; packing_list triggers when activities are ready and weather is done.

On agent failure, the event is still emitted with "error": true in the data so the frontend can show "not available" rather than hang.

docs.text: Same as /api/search but waits for all agents and returns a single JSON response. For testing only — too slow for production use.

docs.title: POST /api/discover
docs.text:
The "Surprise Me" endpoint. Given a traveller profile, returns 5 curated destination suggestions without needing a specific destination input.

Auth required: Yes

Request body:

{
  "origin": "JFK",
  "nationality": "American",
  "departure_date": "2026-08-01",
  "return_date": "2026-08-08",
  "budget_usd": 3000,
  "interests": ["food", "history"],
  "adults": 1,
  "children": 0,
  "seniors": 0,
  "infants": 0
}

return_date is optional (for one-way or open-ended trips).

Response:

{
  "destinations": [
    {
      "city": "Lisbon",
      "country": "Portugal",
      "estimated_cost_usd_low": 1400,
      "estimated_cost_usd_high": 2200,
      "visa_type": "visa-free",
      "visa_verified": true,
      "weather_emoji": "☀️",
      "weather_description": "Warm and sunny, 22–26°C in August — typical for the season",
      "flight_duration_hours": 7.5,
      "flight_duration_label": "~7h 30m from New York",
      "match_reasons": ["Exceptional food scene", "Rich Age of Discovery history"],
      "highlights": ["Alfama district", "Sintra", "Belém Tower"]
    }
  ]
}

visa_verified: true means the visa type was confirmed from the authoritative _VISA_TABLE lookup. visa_verified: false means the AI's guess was not verifiable — the frontend shows an amber "Verify" badge.

Errors: - 422 — missing required fields - 504 — agent timed out (> 30 seconds); retry - 500 — agent failed; retry

Results are cached in memory for 30 minutes per unique request.

docs.title: POST /api/compare/destination
docs.text:
Lightweight summary of one destination, used by the Search page's Compare mode (one call per destination, in parallel). Runs flights, hotels (no URL enrichment), weather and visa concurrently with per-piece timeouts.

Auth required: Yes

Request body: a TravelSearchRequest for a single destination. destinations must be null or have at most one entry; multi-city requests return 422 ("Compare works with single destinations").

Response (200) — example for 2 adults, 7 nights, budget_usd: 3000:

{
  "destination": "Lisbon, Portugal",
  "label": "Lisbon",
  "flight": {"price_usd": 620, "stops": 0, "duration_minutes": 895, "airline": "TAP Air Portugal", "source": "google_flights"},
  "hotel": {"typical_nightly_usd": 110, "cheapest_good_nightly_usd": 70, "count": 5},
  "weather": {"avg_high_c": 24.4, "avg_low_c": 15.7, "poor_days": 1, "total_days": 7, "source": "open-meteo"},
  "visa": {"visa_type": "visa-free", "max_stay_days": 90, "fee_usd": 0, "processing_time": "Not required", "verified": true},
  "ease": {"total": 80, "grade": "green", "safety": 18, "english": 15, "infrastructure": 17, "visa_ease": 10},
  "daily_cost_usd": 100,
  "estimate": {
    "total_usd": 1320,
    "flight_usd": 620,
    "stay_usd": 385,
    "daily_usd": 700,
    "included_in_daily": true,
    "nights": 7,
    "partial": false,
    "budget_status": "under"
  },
  "missing": []
}

Any piece that failed or timed out is null and its name is listed in missing; ease/daily_cost_usd are null for destinations outside the static tables. flight.source of estimate marks a non-live fare; visa.verified is true only for static-table data. ease.grade is green (≥ 71), amber (41–70) or red (≤ 40).

Estimate (per traveller): flight_usd is the cheapest fare (flight.price_usd, round trip, per person). daily_usd = daily_cost_usd × days (days = nights, min 1; nights default to 7 without a return_date). daily_cost_usd is an all-in daily budget that already includes lodging, so when it is known total_usd = flight_usd + daily_usd and stay_usd is shown for reference only (included_in_daily: true) — above, 620 + 700 = 1320. When the daily figure is unknown, total_usd = flight_usd + stay_usd and included_in_daily is false. stay_usd = typical nightly × nights × rooms ÷ travellers, with rooms = ⌈(adults + seniors) ÷ 2⌉ (falling back to ⌈num_travelers ÷ 2⌉) — above, 110 × 7 × 1 ÷ 2 = 385. partial is true when the flight or the daily figure is unknown; the total then sums only the known parts. budget_status compares total_usd × num_travelers with budget_usd (the party's budget): over, under (only for a complete estimate), or null with no budget or when a partial total is still within it.

Errors: 422 for multi-city or invalid requests; 502 when every piece failed.

Caching: only complete results (empty missing) are cached in the shared TTL cache, keyed on the full request; partial results and 502s are never cached.

docs.title: Section Endpoints
docs.text:
Each results section is also exposed as a standalone endpoint (same request body as /api/search, plus per-domain filters):

Endpoint Returns POST /api/flights Flight options (supports stop/price/time filters; multi-city returns ordered legs). With live fares (SerpAPI) a single-city result may also carry price_insights POST /api/flights/fare-calendar Cheapest live fare for departure dates ±3 days (see below) POST /api/hotels Hotels across four budget tiers (bed/price/wifi/distance filters) POST /api/activities Interest-ranked activities (category/price/date/rating filters) POST /api/visa Entry requirements for the traveler's nationality POST /api/sim SIM/eSIM plans POST /api/tips Safety, culture & practical tips POST /api/getting-around Local + inter-city transportation options POST /api/forex Currency & money guidance POST /api/itinerary Day-by-day itinerary POST /api/events What's On — festivals, concerts, exhibitions during the trip POST /api/layover Layover excursion plan for long connections POST /api/stress-test Adversarial itinerary health check (pacing, timing, visa deadlines, weather, budget) POST /api/walking-tours Free walking tours crawled from GuruWalk, FreeTour.com, FreeWalkingTour.com and SANDEMANs NewEurope

docs.title: Flight price_insights
docs.text:
When flights come from Google Flights (SerpAPI) on a single-city trip, the result may include Google's own price verdict, taken from the outbound search response (no extra calls). Fields are kept only when well-formed; the object is omitted when there is no usable price_level or lowest_price. Model-generated flight results never carry it (stripped like live_fare), and it does not change the section's verification label.

"price_insights": {
  "lowest_price": 512,
  "price_level": "low",
  "typical_price_range": [600, 820],
  "price_history": [[1727740800, 650], [1727827200, 512]]
}

price_level is low, typical or high.

docs.title: Airport codes for live flights
docs.text: Live flight search (/api/flights, the search stream and the fare calendar) needs airport codes. The request validator sets them from origin / destination: a bare three-letter code is used as typed; a UI label whose code prefix is in the airports DB ("LGW — London, United Kingdom") uses that code alone (an unknown prefix stays part of the text); any other text ("Berlin", "Berlin, Germany") is looked up by exact city name in the local airports DB (lookup_city_iata, one indexed query, never a web lookup). The city is also tried accent-folded (core/places.fold_place: "Zürich", "São Paulo", "Kraków", "Alesund" → "Ålesund"), with its other St / St. / Saint spellings ("St Louis", "Saint Petersburg"), and through CITY_ALIASES ("Washington" / "Washington DC" → Washington D.C., "Saigon", "Bombay", "New York City"). A last comma segment restricts the match when it is recognised: a country name, ISO code or common alias such as "UK" keeps that country's airports; a region code or full region name from core/places.py (US states, Canadian provinces, Australian and Brazilian states; accent-folded, so "São Paulo, São Paulo" works) keeps the airports in that region, in a country that region can be in (db/airport_regions.py gives the regions of every seeded US, Canadian, Australian and Brazilian airport; MCI is both Missouri and Kansas): "Portland, OR" → PDX, "Portland, Maine" → PWM, "Victoria, British Columbia" → YYJ, "Perth, WA" → PER (Washington or Western Australia), and "San Jose, CA" reads CA as California while "Toronto, CA" reads it as Canada. A city whose airports lie in more than one region and no region given ("Portland") resolves to nothing. An unrecognised segment ("Munich, Bavaria") is ignored. Web-saved airport rows (no country_code) count only when no seeded row matches the city. Up to 3 airports are sent comma-joined, primary first ("London" → LHR,LGW,STN); the booking link uses the first. A city that is unknown, not in the stated country ("Paris, Texas") or in more than one country with no country given resolves to nothing, and flights fall back to AI estimates.

docs.title: POST /api/flights/fare-calendar
docs.text:
Auth required (401 without a valid token); light_ai rate-limit bucket. Body: the same TravelSearchRequest as /api/search.

For each departure date from 3 days before to 3 days after the requested one, it makes one Google Flights outbound search (SerpAPI) with the return date shifted by the same amount, so the trip length stays the same, and takes the cheapest price (for a round trip that is already the round-trip total). There are no return-leg calls, so this is at most 7 calls, run 4 at a time. Overlapping requests for the same dates (a second tab, a double-mounted component) share the lookups already in flight, so each date costs one call. Dates before tomorrow are skipped. An unfiltered main flight search stores its own cheapest outbound-stage price as the calendar entry for its dates. The requested date shows the lower of that price and the cheapest flight card of the cached main search, so it matches the cards (the main round-trip search always return-prices the lowest-priced outbound, wherever Google lists it, plus the earliest and latest departures); Google's price_insights.lowest_price is used only when neither is available. Each date's price is cached for 30 minutes (serp-cal:{origin}:{dest}:{dep}:{ret}:{travelers}). A date that fails for any reason (HTTP error, timeout, unreadable response) or has no flights comes back as null; the calendar as a whole never fails, and failures are not cached.

{
  "dates": [
    {"departure_date": "2026-10-31", "return_date": "2026-11-07", "cheapest_usd": 610.0, "is_selected": false},
    {"departure_date": "2026-11-03", "return_date": "2026-11-10", "cheapest_usd": 565.0, "is_selected": true},
    {"departure_date": "2026-11-04", "return_date": "2026-11-11", "cheapest_usd": null, "is_selected": false}
  ],
  "currency": "USD",
  "source": "google_flights"
}

Errors (string detail):

Status When 401 Not signed in 422 Multi-city request ("Fare calendar is only available for single-destination trips.") or invalid body 429 Rate limit (see above) 503 {"detail": "Fare calendar needs live flight data, which isn't configured."} — SERPAPI_KEY is not set

docs.title: POST /api/walking-tours
docs.text:
Free and pay-what-you-wish walking tours at the destination (every stop on multi-city trips). Tours are crawled from the providers' public city pages; the LLM only chooses and explains them by id, so every url is a real provider tour page. Same request body as /api/search.

{
  "origin": "NYC",
  "destination": "Lisbon, Portugal",
  "departure_date": "2026-04-01",
  "return_date": "2026-04-08",
  "interests": ["history", "food"],
  "num_travelers": 2
}

Response:

{
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "t3",
      "name": "Lisbon Old Town Free Walking Tour",
      "provider": "GuruWalk",
      "provider_key": "guruwalk",
      "url": "https://www.guruwalk.com/walks/...",
      "image_url": "https://...",
      "description": "Alfama, the cathedral and the viewpoints, with a local guide.",
      "rating": 4.9,
      "review_count": 1280,
      "duration": "2h 30m",
      "price_note": "Free (tip your guide)",
      "city": "Lisbon",
      "reason": "Covers the old-town history you asked for.",
      "top_pick": true
    }
  ],
  "sources": [
    {
      "provider": "GuruWalk",
      "provider_key": "guruwalk",
      "city": "Lisbon",
      "url": "https://www.guruwalk.com/lisbon",
      "count": 6,
      "status": "ok"
    }
  ]
}

sources has one entry per provider and city; status is ok, none (page found, no free tours) or error. Each city is topped up to at least min(4, available) tours. The endpoint returns {"error": ...} only when every provider fails.

docs.title: GET /api/taste-profile
docs.text: Returns the authenticated user's learned taste profile — signals mined from saved-plan selections (flight style, hotel tier, activity categories, budget band) plus the natural-language summary injected into agent prompts. DELETE /api/taste-profile resets it.

docs.title: POST /api/analytics/events
docs.text: Ingests batched client-side usage events (up to 50 per call). Returns 204.

docs.title: Reference Data
docs.text: Endpoint Returns GET /api/airports?q= Airport/city typeahead search GET /api/nationalities?q= Nationality typeahead search

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text: Liveness check. Returns {"status": "ok", "service": "travel-planner-backend", "serpapi_configured": true|false}; the Results page reads serpapi_configured once per page load to decide whether to offer the fare calendar. Used by Cloud Run health probes and Cloud Monitoring uptime checks. No auth required.

docs.title: Agent System
docs.text: Travel Planner's AI capabilities are built on a lightweight agent framework. This page explains how the framework works, how agents are defined, what each specialist agent does, and how the system handles failures.

docs.title: BaseAgent
docs.text:
Every agent inherits from BaseAgent (backend/app/agents/base_agent.py). It handles:

  1. Loading the agent definition — reads .agents/{name}.md, parses the YAML frontmatter, and stores the system prompt body
  2. Building the conversation — constructs the messages array with the system prompt and a user message derived from the search context
  3. Calling Claude — uses claude-agent-sdk with configurable model, max_tokens, and max_turns from frontmatter
  4. Retrying on failure — up to 4 attempts with exponential backoff
  5. Parsing the response — applies a 3-strategy JSON extraction fallback
  6. Returning a typed result — all agents return a Pydantic model, never raw dicts

docs.title: Agent definition format
docs.text:
Agent prompts live in .agents/ at the project root. Each file is a markdown document with YAML frontmatter:

---
name: flights
description: Finds typical flight routes, airlines, and price guidance
tools: []
max_turns: 1
---

You are a specialist travel flights analyst...

Frontmatter fields:

Field Type Description name string Agent identifier, must match the filename description string Human-readable description, used in logs tools list Tool-use configuration; most agents use [] (no tools) max_turns int Maximum conversation turns passed to the SDK

Changing agent behaviour means editing the .md file — no Python changes needed.

docs.title: Retry and JSON parsing logic
docs.text:
Retry: Each agent wraps its API call in a retry loop with up to 4 attempts. On rate limits, server errors, or network timeouts, it waits with exponential backoff. On the 4th failure, it returns a structured error result instead of raising an exception.

JSON parsing (3-strategy fallback):

  1. Direct parse — json.loads() on the full response text
  2. Code block extraction — extract content from ```json ... ``` fences
  3. Regex extraction — find the first {...} block via regex

If all three fail, the agent returns a fallback error result, which the frontend renders as a "not available" section.

docs.title: Phase 0 — Static data (instant)
docs.text:
Static lookup tables in static_results.py yield results before any AI call:

  • VisaAgent.static() — visa category from _VISA_TABLE keyed by (nationality, destination)
  • SimAgent.static() — SIM options by destination
  • TipsAgent.static() — travel tips by destination
  • GettingAroundAgent.static() — transport options by destination
  • get_static_emergency_card() — emergency numbers from _EMERGENCY_NUMBERS (40+ destinations)
  • get_confidence_score() — safety / visa / budget / infrastructure score from _DESTINATION_SCORES (49 destinations)

All stream to the browser within 1 second with source: 'static'. The UI shows them as "Enhancing…" until AI results arrive.

Destinations are matched to a table country by whole names only (_place_country): a stated country wins; otherwise the city map, when a trailing state or region name, or an ISO / region code with a reading in the mapped country, agrees with it ("Miami, FL", "Berlin, DE", "Perth, WA", "Toronto, ON" resolve; "Paris, TX", "Paris, Texas" and "Paris, US" get no row). A known city with an ISO code for another country that is not a US state code takes that country ("Cartagena, ES" → Spain). For a city not in the map, a code resolves only when it has a single reading across ISO codes and the region codes in backend/app/core/places.py (US states, Canadian provinces/territories, Australian and Brazilian states): "Trondheim, NO" → Norway, "Austin, TX" → USA, but "Leipzig, DE", "Fremantle, WA" and "Smalltown, PA" get no row. The city map includes common US, Australian, Canadian and Brazilian cities so "Denver, CO", "Perth, WA" or "Belém, PA" resolve. Names are accent-folded (core/places.fold_place, so "Zürich" and "São Paulo, BR" match) checked under their other St / St. / Saint spellings and through CITY_ALIASES ("Saigon", "Bombay", "Washington D.C."); "Washington, D.C." also resolves to the USA. Full Canadian, Australian and Brazilian state/province names count like their codes ("Sydney, New South Wales", "São Paulo, São Paulo"), and give an unknown city its country ("Victoria, British Columbia" → Canada).

docs.title: Phase 1 — Parallel AI agents
docs.text:
Thirteen agents run concurrently (the phase1_agents dict in the orchestrator), plus two deferred agents. As each finishes, its result is yielded over SSE:

Agent File Purpose FlightsAgent flights_agent.py Routes, airlines, pricing, booking advice HotelsAgent hotels_agent.py Neighbourhoods and accommodation tiers ActivitiesAgent activities_agent.py Activities with interest-relevance scoring PlacesAgent places_agent.py Landmarks from Serper/Google + Claude synthesis WalkingToursAgent walking_tours_agent.py Free walking tours crawled from provider city pages; the LLM picks and explains them EventsAgent events_agent.py Festivals, concerts, and exhibitions during the trip dates VisaAgent visa_agent.py Entry requirements, documents, fees SimAgent sim_agent.py SIM cards, eSIM, local carriers TipsAgent tips_agent.py Etiquette, safety, health, local knowledge ForexAgent forex_agent.py Currency, exchange rates, payment tips GettingAroundAgent getting_around_agent.py Local and intercity transport WeatherAgent weather_agent.py Forecast for travel dates EmergencyCardAgent emergency_card_agent.py Embassy, hospitals, phrases, local laws PricingAdvisorAgent pricing_advisor_agent.py Price trend + booking timing (deferred) PackingListAgent packing_list_agent.py Personalised packing checklist (deferred)

Deferred tasks (triggered by Phase 1 results, not at start): - pricing_advisor starts when ≥ 3 flight prices are available - packing_list starts when activities are ready AND weather is done (or has failed)

Static-backed agents: If visa, SIM, tips, getting around, or emergency card AI calls fail, the error is suppressed and the Phase 0 static data is retained. Users never see a degraded experience for these sections.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Itinerary synthesis
docs.text: ItineraryAgent starts once both activities and hotels are available. It synthesises a day-by-day schedule with morning / afternoon / evening slots, daily cost estimates, and weather-aware themes. Has a 60-second timeout with a template-based fallback.

docs.title: Source verification labels
docs.text:
Right before every section is yielded, the orchestrator calls _attach_verification(name, data, request, pending=False) (logic in backend/app/services/verification.py; the filtered endpoints /api/{flights,hotels,activities}/filtered attach the same final, non-pending label), which adds data["verification"] = {level, label, summary, checks[], items_verified, items_total, pending} with level one of verified, partial, unverified, conflict. Error results get none. Labels come only from evidence the pipeline already holds, with no extra network calls or LLM passes:

  • Flights: live_fare: true on options mapped from SerpAPI Google Flights (never trusted from LLM output); all live is verified, a mix partial, none unverified.
  • Hotels: enrichment sets link_verified: true when a search result's title (or URL path) contains the hotel's distinctive name words and false for hotels it searched without a match; items beyond the enrichment cap carry no flag and are not counted. Words of the destination city are not distinctive ("Hotel Berlin" does not match a "Hotels in Berlin" listing); a name with nothing distinctive left never matches.
  • Activities / places: the resolvers mark every item they actually search (their top N) with link_checked: true, and totals are counted over those only ("1 of the 5 checked"). A trusted-domain result always upgrades the link, but link_verified: true ("found online by name") is set only when that result's title contains the item's distinctive name words. Places' Tier-1 official-site matches (from Serper Places in PlacesAgent.run) are conservatively left unflagged. Name matching for hotels, activities and places shares services/name_match.py (short names need every distinctive word; longer names at least half, minimum 2). Destination words (and an item's own city on multi-city trips) are removed before anything else, and a name left with only generic words ("hotel", "tour", "city", "museum", …) never matches — "Berlin City Tour" is not evidence for a "Top Berlin Tours" page.
  • The first (pre-enrichment) hotels/activities/places yield is pending: true; if the stream ends before the final label arrives, the client clears pending. Model-supplied link_verified / link_checked are stripped; saved plans drop both flags from their items.
  • Walking tours, weather: verified from provider crawl results and the open-meteo source respectively.
  • Visa, emergency card: the AI result is compared with the static reference table. A visa-type match is verified; emergency numbers are verified only when at least two of police / ambulance / fire were compared and all matched (a single matching number is partial). A differing visa type or emergency number is a conflict that names both values and links the official source. The AI data is never overwritten. No table entry means unverified.
  • Static Phase 0 yields (sim, tips, getting around, forex) are verified as curated reference data; their AI yields, the itinerary, stress test, packing list and pricing advisor are unverified.

docs.title: FlightsAgent
docs.text: Generates guidance on flight options between the user's origin and destination. Covers typical routes, airlines, rough price ranges, and booking timing advice. Does not make live flight API calls — uses Claude's knowledge enriched by web search context.

docs.title: HotelsAgent
docs.text: Breaks down accommodation by neighbourhood and type. Covers the best areas to stay (matched to the user's interests), accommodation categories from budget to boutique, price ranges per night, and booking tips. A nightlife-focused user gets different neighbourhood recommendations than a museum-focused user.

docs.title: ActivitiesAgent
docs.text:
Generates a list of activities, experiences, and attractions. After the agent returns, the backend applies relevance scoring:

  1. sentence-transformers encodes each activity description and the user's interests string into embedding vectors
  2. Cosine similarity is computed between each activity and the interests
  3. Activities are sorted descending by similarity score

This means a "street food and local markets" user sees food-focused activities ranked above generic tourist attractions.

docs.title: PlacesAgent
docs.text:
Surfaces must-see landmarks, temples, museums, viewpoints, and markets using live data. The pipeline:

  1. Calls the Serper /places and /search APIs to fetch Google Maps data and editorial mentions
  2. Sends the raw data to Claude for synthesis into structured results
  3. SerperPlacesResolver enriches the top results with TripAdvisor, Timeout, and Lonely Planet URLs

Falls back to Claude-only results if SERPER_KEY is not configured.

docs.title: WalkingToursAgent
docs.text:
Finds free and pay-what-you-wish walking tours. Unlike most agents it does not ask the LLM for tours. For each destination city, services/walking_tours.py fetches the public city page of GuruWalk, FreeTour.com, FreeWalkingTour.com, and SANDEMANs NewEurope in parallel (JSON-LD Event data for the first two, HTML cards for the others, free or pay-what-you-wish only). It sends a VoyagerTravelPlanner/1.0 User-Agent, uses a 12 s request timeout and caps each city's whole crawl at 15 s. It only fetches the four city-page URL patterns, which were verified as robots.txt-permitted on 2026-10-28. Results are cached per provider and city. When the slug misses, a DuckDuckGo site: search looks for the city page (GuruWalk and FreeTour only); discovery only accepts city pages of those patterns whose slug shares a word with the requested city (or, for non-Latin names, whose listings name that city), never site pages, language roots or /search.

The LLM (Haiku) then picks and explains the best tours by candidate id only — every URL comes from the crawl, never the model. Each city is topped up to at least min(4, available) tours by rating; if the LLM fails, a rating × log(reviews) ranking is used. The agent returns an error only when every provider fails.

docs.title: VisaAgent
docs.text: Entry requirements specific to the user's nationality: visa category (visa-free / on-arrival / e-visa / embassy), application process, required documents, processing times, fees, and any notable conditions.

docs.title: SimAgent
docs.text: Mobile connectivity: local carriers and prepaid SIM data plans, eSIM availability, coverage quality, and where to buy. Notes whether home-country roaming might be better for short trips.

docs.title: TipsAgent
docs.text: Cultural and practical information: local customs and etiquette, safety, health precautions, tipping culture, bargaining norms, dress codes for religious sites, local laws tourists sometimes accidentally break.

docs.title: ForexAgent
docs.text: Currency guidance: local currency and ISO code, current exchange rate context, whether to exchange before travel or at destination, ATM availability and fees, card acceptance, digital payment adoption.

docs.title: GettingAroundAgent
docs.text: Transport at the destination: airport transfer options with price ranges, public transport usage, ride-hailing apps, taxi culture, car rental, and intercity travel for multi-city trips.

docs.title: WeatherAgent
docs.text: Fetches forecast data from the Open-Meteo API using destination coordinates from CITY_COORDS. Returns daily high/low temperatures, weather codes (mapped to emoji), and precipitation probability. Used by the weather section and the Timeline view day headers.

docs.title: EmergencyCardAgent
docs.text:
The safety-critical agent. Given destination and nationality, returns:

  • Emergency phone numbers (police, ambulance, fire, tourist police)
  • The traveller's embassy: address, phone, emergency after-hours line, opening hours
  • Nearby international hospitals with English-speaking staff
  • Ten phonetic survival phrases in the local language
  • Local laws with severity levels (critical / warning)

The backend detects home-country trips and skips the embassy section in that case. The frontend renders a printable card via window.open() — reliable across all browsers and mobile.

Phase 0 provides static numbers (from _EMERGENCY_NUMBERS, 40+ destinations) immediately. AI enrichment adds the embassy, hospitals, phrases, and laws. If AI fails, the static numbers are retained.

docs.title: PricingAdvisorAgent (deferred)
docs.text: Triggers when ≥ 3 flight prices are available. Receives the route, average price, and days until departure. Returns whether current prices are above or below typical, a booking recommendation, historical relative price trend data for the sparkline, and confidence level. Rendered as a banner above the Flights section.

docs.title: PackingListAgent (deferred)
docs.text: Triggers when activities are ready and weather is done. Receives a summarised prompt (destination, duration, weather summary, planned activities, traveller profile). Returns categories — Documents, Clothing, Electronics, Medications, Activity Gear, Destination-Specific — with items marked essential or optional. Saved to My Plan as a persistent checklist with localStorage-backed checkbox state.

docs.title: DiscoveryAgent
docs.text:
Powers the "Surprise Me" flow (POST /api/discover). Given origin, budget, dates, nationality, and interests, suggests five curated destinations with cost range, seasonal weather, visa type, flight duration, match reasons, and highlights.

Visa types are post-processed: the LLM's guess is overridden by _VISA_TABLE lookup when available. If not in the table, the badge shows "Verify" rather than potentially wrong data.

Runs as a synchronous endpoint (not SSE) with a 30-second timeout and in-memory caching.

docs.title: ItineraryAgent
docs.text:
Phase 2 synthesis. Receives activities, hotels, the full search context, and weather data. Generates a structured day-by-day schedule:

  • Day number, date, theme, and city
  • Morning / afternoon / evening activity slots with name, location, duration, estimated cost, notes
  • Daily estimated cost
  • duration_hours on every slot and lat/lng on every slot (neighbourhood or hotel coordinates when no specific place) — the frontend derives estimated times and travel between stops from them (utils/schedule.js). The chat itinerary agent (.agents/chat-itinerary.md, ChatItineraryAgent) asks for the same fields
  • Coordinates for the Timeline map view

60-second timeout with a template-based fallback that distributes activities mechanically.

docs.title: Adding a new agent
docs.text:
1. Create .agents/{name}.md with YAML frontmatter and a system prompt
  2. Create backend/app/agents/{name}_agent.py as a subclass of BaseAgent
  3. Add it to the orchestrator in backend/app/agents/orchestrator.py
  4. Add the SSE event type to AGENT_CONFIG and AGENT_ORDER in ResultsPage.jsx
  5. Write a section component to render the data

docs.title: Multi-city behaviour
docs.text:
When request.is_multi_city is true, agents change behaviour:

Agent Multi-city behaviour flights One search per leg via serp_flights.search_multi_city (parallel one-ways, retry, AI fill for empty legs); results grouped into ordered legs weather Per-stay forecasts (city_stays); LLM fallback parses nested per-city output, assigns cities authoritatively by date range, sorts by stop order hotels / activities / places / events Mandatory per-city quotas; every result tagged with city walking_tours Each city crawled separately; every city topped up to at least min(4, available) tours getting_around Intra-city options per city plus inter-city hops (train/bus/flight) tagged with a city route label visa Evaluates every country on the route itinerary Allocates days per city_stays and visits cities in exactly the user's order — never reorders

The chat assistant (chat_agent.py) is documented separately in Chat Assistant: topic queries are answered from model knowledge only, with specialists as a failure-only fallback; planning requests stream the full pipeline.

docs.title: Chat Assistant
docs.text: The chat (/api/chat, ChatPage.jsx, backend/app/agents/chat_agent.py) is a travel advisor that answers instantly from the model's own knowledge and reserves the specialist agent pipeline for structured planning — or as a last-resort fallback.

docs.title: Answering philosophy: knowledge first, agents last
docs.text:
Topic questions ("do I need a visa for Japan?", "which area of Barcelona is best for nightlife?") are answered purely from the LLM's internal knowledge and stream immediately — no agents run, and the stream closes the moment the answer ends.

The specialist agents run only if the model fails to answer at all:

  • the stream errors out,
  • the response is empty, or
  • the model explicitly refuses ("I don't have information on…", detected by _NON_ANSWER_RE).

Only then does the chat extract trip parameters and run the matched specialists as a fallback. This keeps chat responses fast (~seconds) and conversational, while structured data remains one request away on the Search page.

docs.title: Routing pipeline
docs.text:
Each message passes through an ordered router in ChatAgent.stream():

Step Trigger Behaviour 0 Jailbreak / off-topic patterns Polite refusal — chat only discusses travel 1 Plan commands ("add … to my plan", "show my plan") Plan manipulation + response 1.5 Answer to a pending question (e.g. we asked for the origin) Resumes planning with the new slot filled 2 Planning patterns ("plan a week in Lisbon…") Full comprehensive planning (see below) 3 Topic intents (flights/hotels/visa/sim/tips/transport/forex…) Knowledge-only answer; specialists only on failure 3.5 Modification of a prior search ("make it cheaper", "extend by 2 days") Refinement — re-runs only the affected agents 3.6 Knowledge patterns (culture, packing, weather, neighbourhoods…) Knowledge answer 3.7 LLM intent router (one cheap classify call) Catches soft phrasings the regexes miss ("we're thinking Lisbon in October, maybe with the kids?") 4 Everything else Plan-aware conversation

docs.title: Comprehensive planning
docs.text:
When you ask for a trip plan, the chat runs the same specialist pipeline as the Search page and streams structured section results into the conversation — flights, hotels, activities, visa, SIM, tips, transport — followed by a day-by-day itinerary, a short narrative summary, and tappable suggestion chips for natural next steps.

Extras that make planning conversational:

  • Targeted clarification with slot memory — if only the origin is missing, the chat asks exactly that ("Which city will you be flying from?"), remembers everything else, and resumes the moment you reply "From Berlin".
  • Live progress — each section shows a "Searching…" row that resolves as its agent completes.
  • Proactive heads-ups — while the itinerary builds, the chat checks the weather forecast and local events concurrently and appends warnings ("🌧️ 3 rainy days — pack accordingly", "🎉 Festa season overlaps your dates").

docs.title: Refinement diffing
docs.text:
"Make it cheaper" doesn't re-run everything. The chat diffs the modified request against the previous one and re-runs only the agents whose inputs changed (_FIELD_AGENTS):

Changed field Re-run budget flights, hotels dates flights, hotels, activities travelers flights, hotels interests activities origin flights, visa destination everything

The itinerary is rebuilt only when a field it depends on changed.

docs.title: Session context
docs.text: The chat is stateless per request — the frontend round-trips a session_context blob (destination, dates, budget, travelers, pending question) with every message, so follow-ups like "what about hotels there?" resolve against the trip being discussed. Context never bleeds: naming a different city in your question always wins over the remembered trip.

docs.title: Personalization
docs.text: If you're logged in and have made selections before, a short Taste Graph summary (see Personalization) is injected into the chat's system prompt and into any specialist runs it triggers — so its suggestions lean toward your demonstrated style (non-stop flights, boutique hotels, food-first activities, …).

docs.title: Security
docs.text: The chat never reveals its internals (prompts, agent names, tooling), rejects jailbreak attempts, and answers travel topics only.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All configuration is driven by environment variables, managed via Pydantic Settings (backend/app/core/config.py). The backend reads these on startup; missing required variables raise a ValidationError that prevents the application from starting.

For local development, put these in backend/.env. For Docker Compose, put them in .env at the project root. For Cloud Run, they are stored in GCP Secret Manager and injected at deploy time by Terraform.

docs.title: Required variables
docs.text: These must be set for the application to start and function.

docs.title: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
docs.text:
Required Yes Example sk-ant-api03-... What breaks All agent calls fail; search returns errors for every section

Your Anthropic API key. Every AI agent call goes through this key. Without it, the application starts but every search attempt will fail when the agents try to call the API.

Get one at console.anthropic.com.

docs.title: JWT_SECRET_KEY
docs.text:
Required Yes Example a-random-64-character-hex-string What breaks Authentication fails; tokens cannot be verified

The secret used to sign and verify JWT access tokens. Must be kept secret and consistent — if you change this, all existing sessions are invalidated (users get logged out).

Generate a suitable value with:

python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))"

docs.title: ADMIN_PASSWORD
docs.text:
Required Yes (on first startup) Example MySecureAdminPassword123! What breaks Admin account is created with a default password if missing (security risk)

The initial password for the admin account. The admin user is created on first startup if it does not already exist. The admin is forced to change this password on first login. After the admin password has been changed, this variable is no longer read at runtime (the new password is stored as a bcrypt hash in users.db).

docs.title: DATA_DIR
docs.text:
Required No Default ./data Example /app/data What breaks SQLite database files are created relative to the working directory

The directory where the four SQLite database files (users.db, plans.db, preferences.db, feedback.db) are stored. In Docker and Cloud Run deployments this should point to a writable path. The directory is created automatically if it does not exist.

docs.title: BACKUP_BUCKET
docs.text:
Required No Default None (GCS backup disabled) Example my-travel-planner-backups What breaks SQLite data is not backed up; lost on Cloud Run instance restart

The name of the GCS bucket to use for SQLite backups. If not set, backup is silently disabled and a log message confirms this. Required for any production or Cloud Run deployment where the local filesystem is ephemeral.

GCS authentication uses Application Default Credentials. In Cloud Run, the service account attached to the Cloud Run service must have storage.objects.create and storage.objects.get permissions on this bucket.

docs.title: AGENTS_DIR
docs.text:
Required No Default ./.agents Example /app/.agents What breaks Agents cannot load their system prompts; all agent calls fail with FileNotFoundError

Path to the directory containing .agents/*.md definition files. In Docker images this should be the absolute path where the .agents/ directory is copied. In local development, the default relative path resolves correctly when the backend is started from the backend/ directory.

docs.title: CORS_ORIGINS
docs.text:
Required No Default http://localhost:5174 Example https://travel-planner.example.com,http://localhost:5174 What breaks Browser blocks API requests from your frontend origin

Comma-separated list of allowed CORS origins. In production, set this to your frontend's public URL. In local development, the default covers the Vite dev server (port 5174). In Cloud Run, Terraform sets this to the frontend Cloud Run service URL.

docs.title: Rate-limit variables
docs.text:
AI endpoints are limited per signed-in user (or client IP when anonymous) over a rolling window; see the API Reference for which endpoints fall in which bucket. Over the limit the API returns 429 with a Retry-After header.

Variable Default Meaning RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED true false turns all limits off (the test suite does this) RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS 600 Length of the rolling window RATE_LIMIT_SEARCH 10 /api/search, /api/search/sync per window RATE_LIMIT_CHAT 30 /api/chat per window RATE_LIMIT_COMPARE 30 /api/compare/destination per window RATE_LIMIT_DISCOVER 10 /api/discover per window RATE_LIMIT_LIGHT_AI 60 Single-agent routes, /*/filtered, /api/layover, /api/stress-test per window

Counters live in process memory: they reset on restart and are not shared between instances. Anonymous callers are keyed by the connecting client's address, so behind a reverse proxy all anonymous traffic shares one bucket unless the proxy's address is replaced (e.g. uvicorn --proxy-headers).

docs.title: LOG_FORMAT
docs.text:
Required No Default json Values json, console What breaks Nothing breaks; logs are just harder to read

Controls whether structlog outputs JSON (for log aggregation in Cloud Run / Cloud Logging) or human-readable coloured output (for local development). Set to console when running locally.

docs.title: Search API variables (optional)
docs.text: These are used if you want the agents to perform live web searches to supplement their training data. If not set, agents rely solely on the model's knowledge.

docs.title: SERPER_KEY
docs.text:
Required No Default None Example abc123...

API key for Serper.dev (Google Search API). Used by the PlacesAgent to fetch real-time place data that Claude then synthesises into the places_to_see section. Get one at serper.dev.

If not provided, the application falls back to DuckDuckGo search (no key required) for any web search operations.
