docs.title: Static-first design philosophy
docs.text:
Phase 0 exists because some data does not benefit from being generated by a language model. A lookup table for visa categories is faster, cheaper, and more deterministic than asking Claude whether a German passport holder needs a visa for Thailand. Static data is pre-computed, served instantly, and gives the user something to read while the AI agents run. This also makes the application feel significantly faster than a pure AI approach.

The confidence score (_DESTINATION_SCORES) gives the UI four numeric sub-scores (safety, visa complexity, budget, infrastructure) that render as a dashboard widget while the main content loads.

The same philosophy applies to the ItineraryAgent's template fallback: if the model is slow or unavailable, the application degrades gracefully rather than timing out with an error. The fallback itinerary is built entirely from already-available activities and hotels data with no additional API calls.

docs.title: SSE streaming mechanism
docs.text:
The backend uses FastAPI's StreamingResponse with text/event-stream content type. Every event follows a consistent JSON envelope:

data: {"type": "visa",            "data": {...}, "source": "static"}


data: {"type": "confidence",      "data": {...}, "source": "static"}


data: {"type": "agent_status",    "agent": "flights", "status": "searching"}


data: {"type": "flights",         "data": {...}, "source": "ai"}


data: {"type": "activities",      "data": {...}, "source": "ai"}


data: {"type": "packing_list",    "data": {...}, "source": "ai"}


data: {"type": "itinerary",       "data": {...}}


data: {"type": "done"}


: keepalive

Key conventions:

  • source: "static" — data came from a lookup table; the UI renders it with an "Enhancing..." badge.
  • source: "ai" — data came from an AI agent; the UI replaces static content and shows "Done".
  • agent_status events — sent before Phase 1 starts, one per agent. The UI uses these to show progress spinners.
  • keepalive comments (: keepalive) — sent every 3 seconds when waiting for slow agents, preventing proxy timeouts.

Each event is flushed immediately. The browser receives and renders sections progressively rather than waiting for the full response.

docs.title: Web Worker pattern
docs.text:
Parsing a high-frequency SSE stream on the browser's main thread risks blocking UI rendering. Travel Planner uses a dedicated Web Worker (sseWorker.js) to handle the SSE connection and parse incoming events off the main thread. Parsed section data is posted back to the main thread via postMessage, where React state updates trigger re-renders. This keeps the UI responsive throughout the streaming period.

The same pattern is used for the chat interface (chatWorker.js), which may trigger the full specialist-agent pipeline if it detects a trip-planning intent in user messages.

docs.title: Deferred tasks
docs.text:
Two agents are not launched at the start of Phase 1. They are triggered mid-Phase-1 as soon as their inputs become available.

PricingAdvisorAgent

  • Trigger: flights result arrives AND contains ≥ 3 entries with price_usd.
  • Inputs: flight results, computed average price, days until departure.
  • Output: booking timing recommendation + SVG sparkline price trend data.
  • Timeout: 45 seconds. If it times out or fails, the section is omitted (no fallback).

PackingListAgent

  • Trigger: activities result arrives AND weather result arrives (or has failed).
  • Inputs: destination, trip duration, traveler context, weather summary (avg high temp + poor-day count), first 8 activity names.
  • Output: categorised checklist — Documents, Clothing, Electronics, Medications, Activity Gear, Destination-Specific.
  • Saved to My Plan; checkbox state persisted in localStorage on the frontend.
  • Timeout: 45 seconds. If it times out or fails, the section is omitted.

Both deferred agents are also started unconditionally at the beginning of Phase 2 as a safety net, in case their trigger conditions were met but not caught during Phase 1 processing (e.g., if the queue was processed very quickly).

docs.title: SQLite + GCS backup strategy
docs.text:
Travel Planner uses four SQLite databases:

Database Contents users.db User accounts, hashed passwords, roles plans.db Saved trip plans per user preferences.db User travel preferences feedback.db User feedback on plans

SQLite was chosen for operational simplicity: no separate database process to manage, no connection pooling, no migrations to coordinate. For the expected scale of this application (hundreds to low thousands of users), SQLite is more than sufficient.

Backup mechanism: A background task runs every 5 minutes and uploads all four database files to a Google Cloud Storage bucket. A SIGTERM handler also triggers a final backup before the process exits (important for Cloud Run deployments, which send SIGTERM before terminating instances).

Restore on startup: On application start, if the local database files are missing or empty (as they will be on a fresh Cloud Run instance), the application downloads them from GCS before accepting traffic. This gives Cloud Run's stateless compute the behaviour of a persistent database.

docs.title: Caching
docs.text:
In-memory caching via cachetools (TTL 30 minutes, max 500 entries). Cache keys are used for:

  • Serper Places API responses (serper:places_ctx:{destination}) — avoids repeated external API calls within a session.
  • Crawled walking-tour listings (walking_tours:{provider}:{slug}) — one entry per provider and city, so a repeat search or another trip to the same city does not re-fetch the provider pages.
  • The cache is shared process-wide, so repeated searches for the same destination within 30 minutes reuse the Serper data and the crawled tours.

docs.title: Why these choices were made
docs.text:
FastAPI over Django/Flask: Native async support is essential for running 13+ concurrent agent calls without blocking. FastAPI's StreamingResponse makes SSE straightforward to implement. The asyncio.create_task + queue pattern allows the orchestrator to stream each result the moment it arrives.

SQLite over PostgreSQL/MySQL: Zero infrastructure overhead. The GCS backup strategy handles durability. Cloud Run's ephemeral filesystem is the only risk, and the backup/restore lifecycle addresses it.

Sentence-transformers for relevance scoring: A deterministic, locally-run semantic similarity model gives meaningful activity ranking without an extra API call. It runs fast enough (< 500ms) to not add noticeable latency to Phase 1.

.agents/*.md for agent definitions: Keeping system prompts as markdown files with YAML frontmatter means prompt engineers can edit them without touching Python code. The frontmatter carries metadata (name, description, tools, max_turns) that the BaseAgent reads at load time.

Web Worker for SSE: The alternative — parsing SSE on the main thread — causes frame drops on low-end devices during peak streaming. The worker approach is a small amount of complexity for a meaningful UX improvement.

Deferred agent pattern: PricingAdvisorAgent and PackingListAgent need data from other agents before they can run. Rather than waiting for all of Phase 1 to finish, they trigger as soon as their inputs are available, hiding their latency behind the remaining Phase 1 agents.

Static-backed agent suppression: For agents with Phase 0 static data (visa, sim, tips, getting_around, forex, emergency_card), an AI failure is silently suppressed. The user already has correct static data on screen; replacing it with an error would be a regression. Both the orchestrator (backend) and the SSE event handler (frontend) enforce this invariant independently.

docs.title: Multi-city execution model
docs.text:
Multi-city trips (destinations: ["Paris", "Rome", "Barcelona"]) reuse the same three-phase pipeline with three derived structures on TravelSearchRequest:

  • city_stays — trip days split proportionally across cities (round(i × days / n) boundaries, exact date coverage for any split). Each stay's end_date is the move-on day.
  • flight_legs — origin → city₁ on the departure date, one inter-city hop per move-on day, last city → origin on the return date.
  • multi_city_context — a prompt block instructing every agent to cover all cities and tag each result with a city field.

Flights run one parallel SerpAPI one-way search per leg (20 s timeout + one retry); legs that still come back empty are AI-filled with estimates so the UI never shows an empty leg. Weather forecasts each stay only for its own dates. Specialist prompts carry per-city minimum quotas (hotels ≥ 3, activities ≥ 5, places 4–6, events 2–4, walking tours ≥ min(4, available) per city).

Journey order is enforced twice: the backend sorts flight legs and weather days into the user's stop order, and the frontend stable-sorts every city-tagged section list by the entered stop order the moment results arrive (orderSectionByCity). The itinerary agent is explicitly forbidden from reordering the route. See Multi-City Trips.

docs.title: Chat design: knowledge-only answers, agents as last resort
docs.text:
Chat topic queries are answered purely from the model's own knowledge and the SSE stream closes as soon as the answer ends. Specialist agents run only when the model fails to answer at all (stream error, empty response, or explicit refusal detected by _NON_ANSWER_RE). Structured planning requests ("plan a week in Lisbon") still run the full agent pipeline and stream section results into the conversation, with refinement diffing re-running only the agents whose inputs changed. See Chat Assistant.

Why: running agents for every chat question made responses feel slow and heavy; a background-verification design held the stream open for up to ~40 s after the answer. Knowledge-only answering keeps chat conversational while the Search page remains the live-data surface.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: Travel Planner is deployed on Google Cloud Platform. The backend and frontend each run as separate Cloud Run services. Infrastructure is managed with Terraform. Deployments are triggered by GitHub Actions.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
GitHub (push to main)
    │
    ▼
GitHub Actions CI/CD
    ├── Build + push backend Docker image → Artifact Registry
    ├── Build + push frontend Docker image → Artifact Registry
    ├── Run terraform plan + apply
    └── Cloud Run services updated with new image tags

Cloud Run (backend)          Cloud Run (frontend nginx)
    port 8001                    port 8080
    ├── FastAPI app              ├── Serves built React SPA
    ├── SQLite databases         └── Proxies /api/* to backend
    ├── GCS backup every 5m
    └── GCS restore on start

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• GCP project with billing enabled
  • gcloud CLI authenticated (gcloud auth application-default login)
  • Terraform >= 1.5 installed
  • GitHub repository with Actions enabled
  • Anthropic API key

docs.title: Step 1: Bootstrap GCP
docs.text:
Before Terraform can run, a few manual one-time steps are needed to create the state bucket and enable APIs.

# Set your project
export PROJECT_ID=your-gcp-project-id
gcloud config set project $PROJECT_ID

# Enable required APIs
gcloud services enable \
  run.googleapis.com \
  artifactregistry.googleapis.com \
  secretmanager.googleapis.com \
  storage.googleapis.com \
  cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com

# Create Terraform state bucket
gsutil mb -l europe-west1 gs://${PROJECT_ID}-tf-state

# Create SQLite backup bucket
gsutil mb -l europe-west1 gs://${PROJECT_ID}-db-backup

docs.title: Step 2: Populate secrets in Secret Manager
docs.text:
Terraform reads these secrets at plan/apply time and injects them into Cloud Run as environment variables. Create them before first Terraform run:

# Anthropic API key
echo -n "sk-ant-api03-..." | gcloud secrets create ANTHROPIC_API_KEY --data-file=-

# JWT secret (generate a strong one)
python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))" | \
  gcloud secrets create JWT_SECRET_KEY --data-file=-

# Admin password
echo -n "YourSecureAdminPassword" | gcloud secrets create ADMIN_PASSWORD --data-file=-

docs.title: Step 3: Configure Terraform variables
docs.text:
Edit infrastructure/terraform/terraform.tfvars:

project_id       = "your-gcp-project-id"
region           = "europe-west1"
backup_bucket    = "your-gcp-project-id-db-backup"
tf_state_bucket  = "your-gcp-project-id-tf-state"

docs.title: Step 4: Add GitHub Actions secrets
docs.text:
In your GitHub repository settings → Secrets and variables → Actions:

Secret Value GCP_PROJECT_ID Your GCP project ID GCP_SA_KEY JSON key for a GCP service account with Cloud Run Admin, Artifact Registry Writer, and Secret Manager Accessor roles

docs.title: Step 5: First deployment
docs.text:
Push to main. GitHub Actions will:

  1. Build the backend image and push to Artifact Registry
  2. Build the frontend image and push to Artifact Registry
  3. Run terraform init and terraform apply — this creates the Cloud Run services, sets environment variables from Secret Manager, and configures IAM
  4. Both Cloud Run services are live

After the first deployment, get the service URLs:

cd infrastructure/terraform
terraform output backend_url
terraform output frontend_url

docs.title: Cloud Run configuration
docs.text:
Backend service:

Setting Value Container port 8001 CPU 2 vCPU Memory 2 GiB Min instances 1 (to avoid cold start delay) Max instances 10 Startup probe GET /api/health/ready Timeout 300s (needed for long SSE streams) Concurrency 80

Frontend service:

Setting Value Container port 8080 CPU 1 vCPU Memory 512 MiB Min instances 0 Max instances 5

The frontend nginx config proxies /api/* to the backend Cloud Run URL. The backend URL is baked into the nginx config at build time via a Docker build argument set by Terraform.

docs.title: SQLite backup/restore lifecycle
docs.text:
On startup (Cloud Run container start):

  1. Application checks for existing database files in DATA_DIR
  2. If any are missing or empty (fresh container), downloads from GCS backup bucket
  3. Startup probe (/api/health/ready) passes only after databases are confirmed accessible
  4. Cloud Run's startup probe retries until the probe passes, so the container does not receive traffic until restore is complete

During runtime:

  • A background asyncio task runs every 5 minutes, uploading all four .db files to GCS
  • Each upload is atomic — the file is written to a .tmp key and renamed, so a partial upload cannot corrupt the backup

On shutdown (SIGTERM from Cloud Run):

  • Cloud Run sends SIGTERM 10 seconds before hard-killing the container
  • A SIGTERM handler triggers an immediate GCS backup before the process exits
  • This ensures the most recent data (up to the last 5 minutes) is preserved even on instance scale-down

docs.title: Monitoring and logging
docs.text:
Cloud Logging: All logs are in JSON format (set via LOG_FORMAT=json) and automatically ingested by Cloud Logging. Use the Log Explorer with filter resource.type="cloud_run_revision" to query logs.

Key log fields (structlog):

Field Description agent Which agent emitted the log phase 0, 1, or 2 duration_ms Agent call duration retry_count Number of retries before success user_id Authenticated user (hashed, not plain)

Cloud Run metrics: CPU utilisation, request count, request latency, and container instance count are available in the Cloud Run console under "Metrics". Set up alerting policies for P99 latency > 40s or error rate > 1%.

docs.title: Rollback procedure
docs.text:
If a deployment introduces a regression:

Option 1: GitHub Actions redeploy

Revert the commit and push to main. GitHub Actions will rebuild and redeploy from the reverted code.

Option 2: Cloud Run traffic split (fastest)

Cloud Run keeps the previous revision. To instantly roll back without a build:

# Find the previous revision name
gcloud run revisions list --service travel-planner-backend --region europe-west1

# Route 100% traffic to the previous revision
gcloud run services update-traffic travel-planner-backend \
  --region europe-west1 \
  --to-revisions PREVIOUS_REVISION_NAME=100

Replace PREVIOUS_REVISION_NAME with the revision from the list output.

Option 3: Database restore

If you need to restore the SQLite databases to a previous state (e.g. after a bad migration):

# List available backups
gsutil ls gs://your-backup-bucket/

# Download a specific backup
gsutil cp gs://your-backup-bucket/users.db.backup ./users.db

Then restart the Cloud Run service with gcloud run services update to trigger a new container start, which will restore from the updated backup.

docs.title: Free Walking Tours Section Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: A new "Free Walking Tours" section on the Results page, right after "Places to See". It recommends free walking tours for each destination city, found by crawling GuruWalk, FreeTour.com, SANDEMANs NewEurope and FreeWalkingTour.com. Every card links to the original tour page.

Architecture: - A deterministic crawler service fetches each provider's public city page, then parses structured data (JSON-LD Event) or HTML cards into one normalized tour shape. - A new specialist agent, WalkingToursAgent, runs the crawl per destination city. It asks the LLM (Haiku, via BaseAgent.execute) to pick and explain the best tours for this traveler, choosing by candidate id only. URLs always come from the crawl and never from the LLM. - If the LLM fails, a rating-based ranking is used, so a successful crawl never yields a blank section. - The agent streams as a normal Phase-1 section (type: "walking_tours"). - The frontend adds a section component plus full My Plan support: drawer, saved-plan viewer, share page and print.

Tech Stack: FastAPI, httpx (async), BeautifulSoup4, ddgs (fallback discovery), pytest; React 18, Tailwind, vitest (+ jsdom).

Spec: the user request and the design in this conversation, summarised in "Design facts" below.

docs.text:
Provider key Display name City page Parse Notes guruwalk GuruWalk https://www.guruwalk.com/{slug} JSON-LD @type: Event (≈10/page): name, url, image, description, aggregateRating{ratingValue, reviewCount}, offers{price:0} robots disallows /search; city pages allowed freetour FreeTour.com https://www.freetour.com/{slug} JSON-LD Event, same fields robots allows user-initiated agents; only /company/, /booking/, /account/ disallowed freewalkingtour FreeWalkingTour.com https://freewalkingtour.com/{slug}/ HTML cards a.relative.block.h-full (href /{slug}/{tour}/); card text e.g. "Pay what you wish Welcome to Barcelona: Old Town and Modernism 4.9 116 reviews 2h 30m Book now"; image src may be relative /_ipx/... Keep only cards containing "Pay what you wish" (others are paid private tours). Unknown city → HTTP 500 sandemans SANDEMANs NewEurope https://www.neweuropetours.eu/sandemans-tours/{slug}/ a[href*="/sandemans-tours/{slug}/"] with link text; keep titles containing "free" (case-insensitive), dedupe by href Paid "Private Tour" links must be dropped
  • Unknown cities return 404 (or 500 on freewalkingtour). Treat any non-200 response as status "none" for that provider.
  • Requests use the honest User-Agent VoyagerTravelPlanner/1.0 (trip-planning assistant; fetches city tour listings on behalf of a user). It is accepted by all four sites.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• The section key is walking_tours everywhere: SSE type, AGENT_ORDER, selections key, agent name and .agents/walking_tours.md.
  • It is placed immediately after places_to_see in AGENT_ORDER and in the orchestrator lists.
  • LLM output never supplies URLs. The prompt says so, and the code ignores any URL the LLM returns. Card links are crawled URLs whose host matches the provider's domain.
  • Agent prompts always pair each city with its country (repo rule; see docs/agents.md "How to add a new agent").
  • Fetch only the four city-page URL patterns above. One request per provider per city, timeout 12 s, all providers in parallel, results cached in get_cache() under walking_tours:{provider}:{slug}.
  • Chat is knowledge-only: no chat wiring.
  • No new dependencies (httpx, bs4 and ddgs are already in backend/requirements.txt).
  • Frontend links use target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" and pass through safeUrl (exported from frontend/src/utils/planPrint.js).
  • Copy: section label Free Walking Tours; badge label Walking Tours; price notes are Free · tip-based (guruwalk, freetour, sandemans) and Pay what you wish (freewalkingtour).

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. Destination formats. "Tokyo, Japan (HND)", "Kraków" (diacritics), "New York City" and a bare IATA code all need a usable slug, plus discovery when the slug misses. → test_city_slug_* and test_split_city_country_* in Task 1, and test_discovery_fallback_used_on_404 in Task 2.
  2. Malformed provider pages. Broken JSON-LD, missing fields, non-numeric ratings, relative image URLs or HTML changes must yield fewer cards, never a crash or an error for the whole section. → test_parse_*_tolerates_* in Task 1.
  3. LLM misbehaviour. Unknown ids, duplicate ids, invented URLs, an {"error"} result or empty recommendations. Cards must still show (heuristic fallback), with only crawled URLs. → test_agent_* in Task 3.
  4. Partial outages. One or more providers time out or are blocked: the section shows what was found. Only a total failure is an error. → test_fetch_city_tours_partial_failure and test_all_providers_fail_returns_error in Tasks 2–3.
  5. Untrusted links in the UI. A javascript: or other-domain URL in data must not render as a live link. → walking tours card never renders unsafe links in Task 5.

docs.title: Task 1: Provider parsers and city helpers (pure functions)
docs.text:
Files: - Create: backend/app/services/walking_tours.py - Test: backend/tests/test_walking_tours_parsers.py, with small handwritten HTML fixtures inline in the test (mirroring the structures in Design facts; never committed copies of the real pages)

Interfaces — Produces: - PROVIDERS: dict[str, dict] keyed by provider key, each holding name, domain, city_url: Callable[[str], str], price_note - city_slug(city: str) -> str: NFKD → ASCII; lowercase; anything outside [a-z0-9] becomes a single -; strip leading and trailing - - split_city_country(destination: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]: drops a trailing (XXX) IATA code, splits on the first comma, strips whitespace - parse_jsonld_tours(html: str, provider_key: str, city: str) -> list[dict] - parse_freewalkingtour(html: str, slug: str, city: str) -> list[dict] - parse_sandemans(html: str, slug: str, city: str) -> list[dict] - All parsers return tour dicts in the data-contract shape, with id = f"{provider_key}-{slug}-{n}", reason=None, top_pick=False. They keep only URLs whose host equals or ends with the provider domain, cap at 10 tours, drop duplicate URLs, and never raise (they return [] on garbage).

docs.title: Best-Value Package Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: A "Best-value package" card on the Results page that picks a sensible, cheap set of real results (flight, hotel, activities, free walking tour, free places, SIM) and adds them all to My Plan in one click, with Undo.

Architecture: Pure, rule-based derivation in the browser from the results already streamed (results[agent]): no new agent, no backend change. A pure module builds the package and merges it into selections; a presentational component renders it; ResultsPage computes it with useMemo once the search is done and applies it with one setSelections call.

Tech Stack: React 18, Tailwind 4, lucide-react icons, vitest + jsdom (no testing-library; createRoot + act).

Spec: Backlog item #26 in Future_Improvements.md ("Virtual Interlining and Package Deals" → "Best Value Package" card). Design decisions below were made by Claude (user delegated all choices); facts about data shapes come from /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rupak-travel-planner/6a423640-de0e-4ae7-a160-af5d4cd4d6e9/scratchpad/research-26.md.

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Options weighed: (a) a new LLM agent that composes a package — rejected: extra latency and cost, and it could recommend items that are not in the results; (b) deterministic rules over the streamed results — chosen: instant, testable, and every pick is a real listed item with a link.

Pick rules (all numbers coerced with Number() + Number.isFinite; anything non-finite is "unknown"; any results[x] that has an error key or no list is treated as empty):

  • Flight (single-city: results.flights.results; multi-city: each results.flights.legs[i].results, one pick per leg). Candidates: price_usd > 0. If any candidate has source !== 'estimate', drop the 'estimate' ones. Let P = cheapest price. Pool = candidates with price ≤ P × 1.15. Sort pool by total stops asc ((outbound?.stops ?? stops ?? 0) + (return?.stops ?? 0)), then total duration asc (outbound?.duration_minutes ?? duration_minutes + return?.duration_minutes, unknown last), then price asc. Reason: "Cheapest fare" if its price equals P, else "Fewer stops or shorter for $D more than the cheapest fare" (D rounded).
  • Hotel (one only — selections.hotel holds a single hotel). Candidates: price_per_night_usd > 0. Multi-city (searchData.destinations?.length > 1): restrict to hotels whose city equals searchData.destinations[0] when any match. Stars = Math.round(star_rating). Pool = stars 3; if empty stars 4; if empty all candidates. Sort by review_score desc (unknown last), then nightly price asc. Reason: "Mid-range (3★), best-reviewed in its class" (use the actual star count; add the city name for multi-city).
  • Budget fit. If searchData.budget_usd > 0 and the package total is over budget, swap the hotel for the cheapest candidate (same city restriction) whose review_score is unknown or ≥ 7, if that is cheaper; reason becomes "Cheaper stay to fit your budget". Do nothing else to fit the budget.
  • Activities. Candidates: price known and 0 ≤ price ≤ 30. Sort by similarity_score desc (unknown last), then price asc. Up to 3 per city (a.city ?? ''), 6 overall. Reason: "Free" or "$12", plus " · matches your interests" when similarity_score >= 0.5.
  • Free walking tour. One per city (top_pick first, then highest rating), 3 overall. Reason: the tour's price_note.
  • Free places to see. admission_fee_usd coerces to exactly 0; top 2 by rating per city, 4 overall. Reason: "Free entry".
  • SIM. Candidates from results.sim.plans with price_usd > 0. Trip days = whole days between departure and return + 1 (null when either date is missing). Prefer plans with validity_days unknown or ≥ trip days; cheapest of those, else cheapest overall. Reason: "Covers your N-day trip" or "Cheapest plan".
  • Not included: events, getting-around, tips, itinerary slots.
  • No package (return null) unless it has a flight or a hotel.
  • Total = computePlanCost(pkg.selections, searchData) and budget = getBudgetStatus(total, searchData.budget_usd), so the card matches the My Plan drawer exactly. The card states "Flight prices are per person" (same convention as the flights section).

Applying: - One setSelections merge (never repeated handleSelect: its toggles would remove already-picked items). flight, hotel, sim are replaced; multi-city flights replace only the legs the package covers; activities, places_to_see, walking_tours are unioned without duplicates (identity: name, name, url). Nothing else is touched. - If the package will replace a different flight, hotel or SIM the user already picked, the card says so before they click ("Replaces your current hotel and SIM."). - After applying: button shows "Added to My Plan" (disabled) plus Undo, which restores the exact selections from just before the click. The undo snapshot is cleared by a new search/remix. - While a saved plan from the drawer is open (loadedPlanSearchData is non-null), applying is disabled with a short reason, because the open plan may be a different trip. - Placement: Results page, directly after "Remix this trip", only when isDone; it recomputes when results change (filters re-stream sections). - Analytics: track('best_value_package_applied', 'results', { items }) and track('best_value_package_undone', 'results', {}).

Non-goals: ChatPage (chat is knowledge-only), saved-plan viewer, share page, backend changes, per-traveller multiplication of prices (the drawer doesn't do it either).

docs.text:
1. Junk prices ("varies", null, "120" as a string, NaN) — must never produce NaN/$0 totals or pick an unknown-price activity as "Free".
  2. Multi-city results (results.flights.legs, items with city) — one flight per leg, hotel from the first city, per-city caps.
  3. Re-applying / partial overlap with existing picks — no duplicates, no removal of the user's own picks.
  4. Sections that errored ({ error: '...' }) or are missing — package still builds from the rest, or is null.
  5. Undo after the user changed something else in between — Undo restores the pre-click snapshot (documented, accepted trade-off), and is gone after a new search.

docs.title: Drag-and-Drop Itinerary Editing Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: On the Results page itinerary, let users move an activity to another day or time of day (drag-and-drop, plus a keyboard/touch "Move to…" menu), swap two activities, remove one, undo, and reset — with every edit, note, plan pick, export, print view, share page and saved plan following the activity to its new place.

Architecture: A pure layout overlay selections.itinerary_layout records only where each moved/removed activity now sits, keyed by the activity's original slot key ("<day_number>-<time_of_day>", the de-facto ID the whole app already uses). One pure function, arrangeItinerary(itinerary, layout), turns the original itinerary plus the overlay into the arranged days; every reader renders those arranged days and looks up edits/notes by slot.key (the original key), so nothing is re-keyed on a move. The overlay carries a fingerprint of the itinerary it was made for and is ignored when it doesn't match (stream retry, a saved plan for another trip).

Tech Stack: React 18, native HTML5 drag-and-drop (no new library — the codebase already uses native DnD), Tailwind 4, vitest + jsdom (createRoot + act).

Spec: Backlog item #12 in Future_Improvements.md ("Drag-and-Drop Itinerary Editing"). Facts: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rupak-travel-planner/6a423640-de0e-4ae7-a160-af5d4cd4d6e9/scratchpad/research-12.md. All design choices below are Claude's (the user delegated them).

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Options weighed: - (a) Overlay of positions keyed by original slot key — chosen. Edits/notes/plan picks/.ics UIDs (slot-${key}) stay attached to the activity with zero re-keying; old saved plans need nothing; one function to test. - (b) Rewrite selections.itinerary and re-key edits/notes/itinerary_slots on every move — rejected: every move mutates four structures, .ics UIDs change (calendar duplicates), and the live Results itinerary is not selections.itinerary. - (c) A DnD library (dnd-kit) — rejected: new dependency; native DnD is the codebase convention and the "Move to…" menu covers touch/keyboard.

Model: - slotKey(dayNumber, timeOfDay) = \${dayNumber}-${timeOfDay}`. Positions are the three standard timesmorning,afternoon,eveningon each existing day. A slot whosetime_of_dayis not one of the three is displayed where it is and is not movable. -itinerary_layout = { fingerprint: string, positions: { [originalKey]: "-" | null } }—null= removed; a key absent frompositionsstays at its original position.EMPTY_SELECTIONS.itinerary_layout = null. Old plans without it behave exactly as today. -fingerprint= short stable hash of the original itinerary'sday_number|time_of_day|activitylines. A layout whose fingerprint differs from the itinerary being rendered is ignored (rendered as the original) and not written to. - **Move** = put activity A at target position T. If T holds activity B, B moves to A's current position (swap). If T is empty (removed/free), A just moves. Moving to its own position is a no-op. Every day keeps at most one activity per time of day (TimelineView, .ics and print rely on this). - **City rule (multi-city):** a move is allowed only when the source day'scityand the target day'scityare equal (case-insensitive, first comma segment) or either is missing. Swaps must satisfy the rule both ways. - **Remove** = positionnull; the spot shows "Free time" and accepts drops. **Restore** puts a removed activity back at its original position if that is empty, else in the first empty position of its original day, else it stays removed (button disabled with a tooltip). - **Arranged days:** same days, same order and day metadata (date, theme, city); each day's slots = activities now positioned there, sorted morning → afternoon → evening, each slot object is the original slot pluskey(original key) andtime_of_day(its new time).removed: [{ key, slot }]lists removed activities for the UI. - **Costs:** for a day whose contents changed,daily_estimated_cost_usd= sum of its slots' cost (itinerary_edits[key].cost ?? slot.estimated_cost_usd, finite numbers only); untouched days keep the original value.total_estimated_cost_usdis recomputed the same way only when anything changed. Unchanged itinerary → identical numbers to today. - **Plan picks follow:** after every move/remove/restore/undo/reset, eachitinerary_slotsentry is updated to its activity's currentday_number/time_of_day(entries for removed activities are kept, unchanged — the user removes them from the drawer as today). - **Undo:** an in-memory stack of previous layouts (max 20) in ResultsPage; "Undo" reverts the last move/remove/restore. **Reset** clears the layout (with Undo able to bring it back). Both cleared by a new search/remix. - **Where editing happens:** Cards view itinerary only (it is already the edit/notes view). Timeline view, TripMap, drawer, PlanViewModal, SharePage, .ics and print all *display* the arranged itinerary. ChatPage is untouched (chat is knowledge-only; its itinerary is a different shape). - **Health Check:** when the layout has changes, the Trip Health Check section shows one line: "Checked against the original itinerary — your moves aren't re-checked." - **Interaction:** - Each movable slot row has a drag handle (GripVertical,cursor-grab) and isdraggable; drag data uses the custom MIMEapplication/x-itinerary-slot(neverapplication/json, which the drawer treats as a plan). Valid drop targets (other slots and Free-time spots, honouring the city rule) highlight on dragover; invalid ones don't accept the drop. - Each movable slot has a "Move" button opening a small menu listing every valid target as "Day N · Morning" (swaps labelled "Day N · Morning (swap with <activity>)") plus "Remove from day". Fully keyboard operable; Escape closes it; focus returns to the button. - Section toolbar (only when the layout has changes): "N changes" · Undo · Reset. Removed activities listed under "Removed" with Restore. - Status messages in anaria-live="polite"region, e.g. "Moved Sagrada Família to Day 2 · Afternoon". - **Analytics:**track('itinerary_slot_moved', 'results', { method: 'drag'|'menu', swap: bool }),track('itinerary_slot_removed', 'results', {}),track('itinerary_layout_reset', 'results', {})`.

Non-goals: ChatPage itinerary, re-running the Health Check, adding new activities, more than one activity per time of day, editing in Timeline view, backend changes.

docs.title: Trip Comparison Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Let a user compare 2–3 destinations side by side for the same origin, dates and travellers — estimated trip cost, cheapest flight, typical hotel price, weather, visa, safety and ease — then start the full plan for the one they pick with one click.

Architecture: A new lightweight backend endpoint POST /api/compare/destination summarises ONE destination by running only the decision-relevant agents (flights, hotels, weather; visa only when the static table can't answer) in parallel plus the instant static scores, then reducing them to a compact summary with a pure, unit-tested function. The frontend adds a third Search-page mode, "Compare", that fires one request per destination in parallel and fills each column as it arrives.

Tech Stack: FastAPI + Pydantic v2, existing agents (FlightsAgent, HotelsAgent, WeatherAgent, VisaAgent), static tables in backend/app/agents/static_results.py, in-memory TTL cache (backend/app/core/cache.py); React 18 + Tailwind; pytest (asyncio_mode=auto), vitest.

Spec: Backlog item #1 in Future_Improvements.md ("Trip Comparison / Side-by-Side View"). Facts: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rupak-travel-planner/6a423640-de0e-4ae7-a160-af5d4cd4d6e9/scratchpad/research-1-28.md Part A. Design choices are Claude's (user delegated them).

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Options weighed: - (a) Run two or three full /api/search streams side by side — rejected: ~17 LLM calls each through a process-wide semaphore of 6 (each search ~2× slower), minutes of waiting, and the Results page holds only one result set. - (b) Reuse Discover (one LLM call guessing costs) — rejected: estimates only, no real flights/weather; exactly the "is this real?" problem. - (c) Per-destination lightweight summary endpoint — chosen: ~2–3 LLM calls per destination (flights unless SerpAPI is configured, hotels, visa only if not in the static table, weather only for cities Open-Meteo can't serve), real weather, static scores instant; parallel per destination; cacheable per request.

Backend: - POST /api/compare/destination, auth required like other routes, body = TravelSearchRequest (single destination; destinations must be null/≤1 — multi-city is rejected with 422 "Compare works with single destinations"). - Runs concurrently with per-piece timeouts: FlightsAgent.run (45 s), HotelsAgent.run (45 s; no enrich — URLs aren't needed for comparing), WeatherAgent.run (30 s), visa = get_static_visa(request) if it returns data else VisaAgent.run (30 s). A piece that fails or times out becomes null in the summary with its name listed in missing; the endpoint still returns 200 if at least one piece succeeded, else 502. - Summary (pure function summarize_destination(request, flights, hotels, weather, visa, confidence) -> dict in backend/app/services/compare.py): - destination (as given), label (city name: hotels/flights destination string's first comma segment if present, else request.destination) - flight: cheapest valid fare {price_usd, stops, duration_minutes, airline, source} where stops/duration sum outbound + return; price_usd > 0 finite only; prefer non-estimate sources when any exist. null if none. - hotel: {typical_nightly_usd, cheapest_good_nightly_usd, count} — typical = median nightly price of 3★–4★ hotels (fallback all priced hotels); cheapest_good = lowest nightly with review_score >= 7 (null if none). null if no priced hotels. - weather: {avg_high_c, avg_low_c, poor_days, total_days, source} from weather.days; null if no days. - visa: {visa_type, max_stay_days, fee_usd, processing_time, verified} — verified = True only when it came from the static table. - ease: from get_confidence_score(request): {total, grade, safety, english, infrastructure, visa_ease} (sub-score score values); null when the destination isn't in the table. - daily_cost_usd: the table's avg_daily_cost_usd for the destination (expose via a small helper next to get_confidence_score; null when unknown). - estimate: {total_usd, flight_usd, stay_usd, daily_usd, nights} per traveller — flight price + typical nightly × nights + daily cost × days (days = nights, min 1; nights from dates, default 7). Any missing part → that part null and total_usd = sum of known parts with partial: true. budget_status: 'under' | 'over' | null vs request.budget_usd. - missing: list of piece names that failed. - All numbers coerced defensively (strings/junk → ignored). - Cache: key "compare:" + md5(request.model_dump_json()) in the shared TTL cache; store only complete-enough results (≥1 piece) and never cache a 502. - Chat is untouched.

Frontend: - SearchPage mode toggle gains "Compare" (third button). Its form: origin, 2–3 destination fields (AirportSearch; "Add another" up to 3; remove ×), departure/return dates, nationality, budget, travellers, interests — prefilled from the known-mode form/preferences the same way Discover prefills. - On "Compare", one compareDestination(request) call per destination in parallel (new function in frontend/src/services/api.js, axios like the others); each column shows its own loading/error state ("Couldn't load — Retry"). - Comparison table (frontend/src/components/CompareTable.jsx): one column per destination; rows: Estimated trip cost per traveller (with budget chip; "partial" note), Cheapest flight (price · stops · duration · "estimate" badge when source is estimate), Hotel per night (typical / from), Weather (avg high/low °C, "N of M days poor", "climate estimate" when not Open-Meteo), Visa (type, fee, max stay; "Verified" vs "AI — check official site"), Travel Ease (total/100 + grade colour), Safety /20, English /20, Typical daily spend. Per numeric row the best value gets an emerald "Best" marker (lowest cost/price, fewest poor days, highest ease/safety/english); ties mark all; rows with <2 known values mark none. Mobile: columns become stacked cards (no horizontal page scroll at 375px). - Each column has "Plan this trip": switches to known mode with the form prefilled with that destination and the shared fields, and submits it (the normal full search). - Pure helpers in frontend/src/utils/compare.js: buildCompareRequests(form) -> TravelSearchRequest[], bestByRow(summaries) -> { [rowKey]: Set<index> }, formatters. Unit-tested. - Analytics: track('compare_run', 'search', { count }), track('compare_plan_clicked', 'search', { position }).

Non-goals: comparing saved plans, multi-city comparison, chat, sharing a comparison, more than 3 destinations.

For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Every Results section tells the traveller how much to trust it — "Verified" (real source or reference data agrees), "Partly verified" (some items confirmed online), "AI-generated — verify before booking", or "Conflicts with reference" — with the concrete checks behind the label, and hotel/activity/place cards show which items were found online.

Architecture: A pure backend function verify_section(name, data, request) derives a verification object from evidence the pipeline already produces — real data sources (Google Flights, Open-Meteo, crawled walking tours), the web searches enrichment already runs (now recorded per item as link_verified), and the curated static tables (visa, emergency numbers). The orchestrator attaches it to each section's data at every yield (initial, enriched, static), so it streams with the section, is cached with it, and needs no new event type. The frontend renders a chip in each section header with a popover of checks, plus per-item "Found online" badges.

Tech Stack: FastAPI orchestrator (SSE), existing enrichment (backend/app/agents/hotels_agent.py, backend/app/services/activity_url_resolver.py, backend/app/services/places_url_resolver.py), static tables (backend/app/agents/static_results.py); React 18 + Tailwind; pytest, vitest.

Spec: Backlog item #28 in Future_Improvements.md ("Hallucination Guardrails with Source Verification"). Facts: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rupak-travel-planner/6a423640-de0e-4ae7-a160-af5d4cd4d6e9/scratchpad/research-1-28.md Part B. Design choices are Claude's (user delegated them).

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Options weighed: - (a) A second LLM pass that "checks" the first — rejected: an LLM verifying an LLM can hallucinate the verification, adds ~15 calls and latency per search. - (b) New per-item web searches/fetches for every claim — rejected for v1: competes with enrichment for the DuckDuckGo rate limit, fetching LLM-supplied URLs is an SSRF risk, and adds seconds. - (c) Evidence-based labels from data the pipeline already has — chosen: zero added latency or network calls, deterministic and testable, and honest: when there's no evidence the label says so.

verification object (attached as data["verification"] on every yielded section dict that has no error):

{ "level": "verified" | "partial" | "unverified" | "conflict",
  "label": short UI text,
  "summary": one sentence,
  "checks": [ { "label": str, "status": "pass" | "fail" | "info", "detail": str, "url": str | None } ],
  "items_verified": int | None, "items_total": int | None,
  "pending": bool }   # true on the first hotels/activities/places yield while enrichment still runs

Labels: verified → "Verified", partial → "Partly verified", unverified → "AI-generated", conflict → "Check details".

Per section (anything not listed → unverified, summary "Generated by AI from its training data — verify before booking."): - flights: all results source not estimate → verified ("Live fares from Google Flights"); mixed → partial; all estimate → unverified ("Estimated fares — prices change; check the airline"). - hotels: enrichment sets hotel["link_verified"] = True when _search_url matched a listing by name, False when it searched and found nothing (untouched hotels beyond the enrich cap: key absent). verified if all searched found, partial if some, unverified if none; items_verified/items_total over searched hotels; check line "Found online by name: X of N". First (pre-enrich) yield → pending: true, level unverified. - activities: resolver marks link_verified = True on activities it upgraded to a trusted listing domain (getyourguide/viator/klook/tripadvisor/tiqets/musement); partial if any, else unverified with detail "Links are searches, not specific listings". Prices/ratings always an info check "Prices and ratings are AI estimates". Pending on first yield when enrichment will run. - places_to_see: resolver marks link_verified = True when it set info_url from a search result; same partial/unverified logic. - walking_tours: verified ("Listings crawled from the providers' own pages"), one pass check per sources[] entry with status ok (url included); providers that failed → info. - weather: source == 'open-meteo' → verified ("Open-Meteo forecast/climate data"); contains llm-estimate → partial or unverified accordingly. - visa: static-first. Phase-0 static yield → verified, label "Verified", check "Matches our reference table" + official_url. AI yield: if get_static_visa(request) exists — same visa_type (normalised: lowercase, hyphen/space-insensitive) → verified; different → conflict, summary "AI says ; our reference table says . Check the official site.", check status fail with the official_url; never override the AI data. No table entry → unverified ("No reference data for this nationality and destination — confirm on the official site", url = data official_url when present). - emergency_card: compare emergency_numbers.police/ambulance/fire with the static table for the destination when present: all equal → verified; any differ → conflict naming the field and both values; no table → unverified. - static-backed sim / tips / getting_around / forex Phase-0 yields: verified label "Reference data" is NOT used — level verified, label "Verified", summary "From our curated reference data (may lag recent changes)". Their AI yields → unverified. - itinerary, stress_test, packing_list, events, pricing_advisor: unverified (events add an info check per date_certainty distribution, e.g. "3 of 5 dates confirmed annual"). - Error results ({"error": …}) get no verification (unchanged behaviour; cacheability unaffected — never put a key named error in verification).

Orchestrator: one helper _attach_verification(name, data, request, pending=False) called right before every section yield listed in orchestrator.py (Phase 0 static yields, Phase 1 ai yield with pending=True for agents that have enrich, itinerary, stress_test, packing_list (static and ai), pricing_advisor, enriched re-yield with pending=False). Mutating data in place is acceptable only if the same dict isn't reused elsewhere; otherwise copy (implementer checks enrich input reuse).

Frontend: - frontend/src/components/VerificationBadge.jsx: chip (emerald Verified / amber Partly verified / gray AI-generated / rose Check details; "Checking…" spinner when pending), button opening an accessible popover (Escape closes, focus returns) listing checks with pass/fail/info icons and links via safeUrl. - SectionHeader in frontend/src/pages/ResultsPage.jsx renders it for results[agent]?.verification (before the status icons). Static → AI transitions just re-render with the new object. - Per-item "Found online" emerald micro-badge on hotel, activity and place cards when link_verified === true (no badge otherwise — absence is not an accusation). - The section-level conflict also shows as a one-line rose banner inside the Visa / Emergency section body with the official link. - Chat untouched (knowledge-only; chat emitter doesn't call the helper).

Non-goals: new network checks, LLM verifier, chat, exporting labels, changing which data is shown.

docs.title: Backend Hardening: Exact Reference Lookups + Rate Limiting — Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: (1) Reference-table lookups (visa, destination scores, emergency numbers, anything using _match_destination / _find_dest_key in backend/app/agents/static_results.py) match only the right row, so "Verified" labels and Travel Ease scores can't come from a wrong row. (2) Expensive endpoints are rate-limited per user (or per client IP when anonymous) with a clear 429 + Retry-After, and the frontend shows a friendly message.

Architecture: A shared normaliser turns a destination string ("Barcelona, Spain", "BCN — Barcelona, Spain", "tokyo") into candidate place tokens (city, country) and lookups compare whole tokens against table keys and the city→country map — no substring matching in either direction. A small in-process sliding-window limiter (backend/app/core/rate_limit.py) is applied as a FastAPI dependency on expensive routes; limits come from settings; cache hits still count (simplicity) but limits are generous.

Spec: Follow-ups from the 2026-10-29 reviews ("fuzzy static lookups", "no rate limiting anywhere"). Design choices are Claude's (user delegated).

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Lookups: - normalise_place(destination) -> {"city": str|None, "country": str|None, "tokens": set[str]}: lowercase; strip an IATA prefix like "BCN — "; split on commas; first segment = city (or country if it is itself a known country key); last segment = country when ≥2 segments; tokens = whole words/phrases of those segments. - A table key matches when it equals the normalised city, the normalised country, or the country mapped from the city via the existing city→country map (merge the two duplicated maps in _find_dest_key and _match_destination into ONE module-level map). Never key in dest / dest in key. - Nationality matching for _VISA_TABLE: exact match of the normalised nationality (lowercase, trimmed; accept the demonym forms already used in the table) — no substring (tbl_nat in nat is removed). - Behaviour for every currently-correct input must not change: build a regression test over all existing table keys and a list of realistic inputs (city, "City, Country", "IATA — City, Country", country alone, mixed case) asserting the same row as before; plus negative tests that used to match wrongly (e.g. a destination containing a table key as a substring of another word, "Indian" vs "American Indian"-style nationality substrings, short keys like "uk" inside "ukraine", "india" inside "indiana", "niger" inside "nigeria").

Rate limiting: - Sliding-window counter per key user:<username> or ip:<client host>; in-memory, thread-safe enough for asyncio (single process); old timestamps pruned. - Settings (pydantic-settings, env overridable): rate_limit_enabled: bool = True, and per-bucket limits: search 10/10min (POST /api/search, /api/search/sync), chat 30/10min (POST /api/chat), compare 30/10min (POST /api/compare/destination), discover 10/10min, light_ai 60/10min (POST /api/stress-test, /api/{flights,hotels,activities}/filtered and other single-agent POST routes in main.py that call an LLM). - Over the limit → HTTP 429, JSON {"detail": "Too many requests — please wait N seconds and try again."}, header Retry-After: N. - Tests: conftest disables limiting by default (env RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false) so existing tests are unaffected; dedicated tests enable it via settings override and assert 429 + Retry-After after N+1 calls, separate users don't share buckets, window expiry (inject a clock). - Frontend: wherever these calls surface errors — frontend/src/workers/sseWorker.js / services/api.js streamSearch error path, chat worker, compare (compareErrorReason already shows string detail), axios helpers — a 429 shows the server's detail string (no raw JSON). Add/extend unit tests where a helper exists. - Docs: CLAUDE.md (API section note), docs/API-Reference.md (429 behaviour + limits), docs/Configuration.md (settings).

Non-goals: distributed rate limiting, per-plan quotas, changing table contents.

docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: A "Budget planner" panel on the Results page that splits the trip budget into Flights / Stay / Activities / Everything else with sliders, instantly shows which loaded options fit each share, and can fetch cheaper hotels when too few fit.

Spec: Backlog #16 (Future_Improvements.md). Facts: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rupak-travel-planner/6a423640-de0e-4ae7-a160-af5d4cd4d6e9/scratchpad/research-16-18-9.md (#16 section). Choices are Claude's (user delegated).

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Options weighed: (a) slider drives /api/*/filtered (LLM re-run, 3–10 s each) — rejected as the primary mechanism: too slow for a slider and replaces the result lists; (b) client-side caps over already-loaded results — chosen, instant; the existing hotel filter endpoint is used only on demand ("Find cheaper hotels").

Model (pure util frontend/src/utils/budgetPlanner.js, unit-tested, // @vitest-environment node): - Units: the same per-person convention as the My Plan drawer and best-value package (flight price_usd per person; hotel nightly × nights; activity price_usd). Total = searchData.budget_usd (editable in the panel; not saved back to the search). - defaultAllocation(searchData, results) → { flights, stay, activities, other } summing exactly to the budget (integers, remainder to other): flights = cheapest valid fare (min with multi-city legs summed), stay = median nightly of priced hotels × nights, activities = 15% of budget, other = rest; if those exceed the budget, scale flights/stay/activities proportionally so other ≥ 0. No budget → panel hidden. - reallocate(allocation, key, value, total) → moving one category takes from / gives to other first; if other would go below 0, the change is clamped. Total stays constant. - fitResults(results, allocation, searchData) → { hotels: {fits:Set(name), count, total}, flights: {fits:Set(identity), count, total}, activities: {picked:Set(name), spent}, nights }: hotel fits when nightly × nights ≤ stay; flight fits when price ≤ flights (multi-city: per-leg fare ≤ flights share × leg's share of the cheapest total); activities: greedy pick by similarity_score desc (ties price asc) while cumulative price ≤ activities share; free ones always fit. Junk prices are "unknown" → never counted as fitting and never dimmed. - Edge: nights from dates (min 1, default 7) like planHelpers.

UI (frontend/src/components/BudgetPlanner.jsx + test): - Placed directly after the Best-value package card (only when isDone and budget > 0), collapsible (default expanded on desktop, collapsed below 640px). - Editable total (number input) + stacked bar (Flights sky, Stay purple, Activities green, Everything else gray — same colours as CostBreakdown) + three labelled range sliders (step $10) with values and "per person" note; "Everything else" shown read-only with a hint "food, transport, extras". - Under each slider: "6 of 12 hotels fit" / "4 of 9 flights fit" / "Fits 5 activities ($212)". - Toggle "Show only what fits" (default off). Off: over-budget hotel/flight cards are dimmed (opacity) with a small "Over your stay budget" / "Over your flight budget" tag; on: they are hidden with a "N hidden — show all" row. Activities picked by the planner get a "Fits your budget" tag. - When fewer than 3 hotels fit: button "Find cheaper hotels" → calls the existing handleApplyHotelFilters({ max_price_per_night_usd: floor(stay / nights) }) path (existing loading state, badge, verification). - "Reset" restores defaultAllocation. - Allocation state lives in ResultsPage, resets on new search/remix and when results for flights/hotels change (recompute default only if the user hasn't moved a slider). - Best-value package: buildBestValuePackage(results, searchData, { caps }) — when caps provided, hotel candidates limited to those that fit (fallback to current behaviour if none fit) and flight pool limited to fitting fares (fallback likewise); ResultsPage passes caps only when the user has touched the planner. Existing package tests must pass unchanged; add tests for caps. - Accessibility: sliders are <input type="range"> with aria-valuetext "$1,200 for stay"; changes announced politely ("Stay budget $1,200 — 5 of 12 hotels fit"). - Analytics: track('budget_planner_changed', 'results', { key }) (debounced), track('budget_planner_cheaper_hotels', 'results', {}). - Docs: Frontend.md paragraph; CLAUDE.md one line.

Non-goals: saving the allocation in plans, chat, multiplying by travellers, LLM calls from slider moves.

Fare Calendar Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: Show whether today's fares are low/typical/high (from data Google Flights already returns), and an opt-in strip of the cheapest real fare for departure dates ±3 days (same trip length), with one click to re-plan on a cheaper date.

Spec: Backlog #9. Facts: research-16-18-9.md (#9 section). Choices are Claude's.

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Options weighed: (a) LLM-estimated date grid — rejected (fabricated numbers; contradicts the verification rule); (b) 7×7 departure×return grid — rejected (49 SerpAPI calls); (c) price_insights from existing responses (0 extra calls) + opt-in ±3-day departure strip keeping trip length (6 extra calls, cached) — chosen.

Backend: - serp_flights.py: capture price_insights from the outbound search response (lowest_price, price_level, typical_price_range, price_history) and include it in the flights result as price_insights (single-city only); absent → omitted. Not cached separately (rides with the result). Verification for flights unchanged. - New search_calendar(api_key, request, window=3) in serp_flights.py: for each offset in −3..+3 (skip dates before tomorrow; skip offset 0 if the main search result is cached — reuse it), build params via _build_params(request.model_copy(update={departure_date, return_date shifted by the same offset})), ONE outbound call per date (no return-leg calls), cheapest price across best/other flights; concurrency limited (semaphore 4); per-date cache key serp-cal:{origin}:{dest}:{dep}:{ret}:{adults} (30-min TTL, shared cache); a failed date → null price, not an error. - Route POST /api/flights/fare-calendar (auth required like other routes; light_ai rate-limit bucket from the hardening branch if present, else no limiter) body = TravelSearchRequest; 422 for multi-city; 503 {"detail": "Fare calendar needs live flight data, which isn't configured."} when settings.serpapi_key is empty; response { dates: [{ departure_date, return_date, cheapest_usd|null, is_selected }], currency: "USD", source: "google_flights" }. - Tests: mocked _call (no network) — window dates, past-date skipping, null on failure, cache hit, 422/503/401, price_insights passthrough.

Frontend: - Flights section: when results.flights.price_insights exists, a chip under the pricing banner: "Fares are low right now · typical $420–$610" (green/gray/amber for low/typical/high) — real data, linked to the verification idea (no AI). - "Fare calendar" pill in the Flights header actions (next to Filters) shown only when /health reports serpapi_configured (fetch once; cache in module) and the trip is single-city. Click → loads FareCalendarStrip below the banner: 7 cells (weekday, date, price or "—"), cheapest highlighted emerald, selected date outlined, delta vs selected ("−$45"). Loading skeleton; error row with Retry (string detail via existing error helpers; 429 detail shown). - Clicking a different date opens an inline confirm: "Re-plan for Tue 3 Nov – Tue 10 Nov? This runs a new search." → on confirm, runSearch({...searchData, departure_date, return_date}) (existing full search path; selections reset as with Remix) and track('fare_calendar_replan', 'results', { offset }). - Pure helpers in frontend/src/utils/fareCalendar.js (shiftDates, cheapest/delta, formatting) + tests; component FareCalendarStrip.jsx + test. - Fix the PricingAdvisorBanner date bug noted in research (it parses the destination as a date) since we touch this area: use searchData.departure_date. - Docs: API-Reference (endpoint), Frontend.md, CLAUDE.md API table.

Non-goals: multi-city calendars, return-date grid, LLM fallback grid, price alerts.

Goal: Close the four follow-ups parked after PR #17: a US/CA/AU/BR state narrows a city's airports ("Portland, OR" → PDX only), Washington spellings resolve, accented input resolves, and the fare calendar's selected-date price agrees with the flight cards.

Spec: User request 2026-10-30 ("these are things we should explicitly account for and resolve"). Facts gathered by the controller are listed under each item. Choices are Claude's.

docs.title: Facts (verified against the seed and code)
docs.text:
• backend/app/db/seed_airports.py: 544 airports; city names are ASCII-folded ("Sao Paulo", "Zurich", "Montreal", "Krakow", "Reykjavik", "Malmo", "Dusseldorf", "Bogota", "Medellin"); the only non-ASCII city is "Ålesund". No state/region column. US 81, CA 11, AU 11, BR 10 airports.
  • Same-name cities more than 60 km apart: within one country only "portland" (PDX/US, PWM/US, 4070 km); across countries birmingham, san jose, victoria (already None via the country-code ambiguity rule).
  • Washington is stored as city "Washington D.C." (IAD, DCA); BWI is a separate city. "St. Petersburg" is stored with the period; "New York" (JFK, LGA).
  • Fare calendar (serp_flights.search_calendar): non-selected dates use _cheapest(outbound response) (the cheapest price from the first, outbound-stage call). The selected date uses _cached_selected_price(main), which prefers Google's price_insights.lowest_price. Flight cards are return-stage round-trip totals (_map_result on return items). Observed live: selected $360 (lowest_price) vs cheapest card $341.

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
1. State/region narrows airports (lookup_city_iata):
  2. Add a curated AIRPORT_REGION: dict[str, str] (IATA → region code: US state / CA province / AU state / BR UF, lower-case 2–3 letters matching core/places.py region codes) covering every US, CA, AU and BR airport in the seed. A completeness test fails when a seed airport in those countries has no region. Put the map next to the seed data (e.g. backend/app/db/airport_regions.py); no DB schema change.
  3. When the stated last segment is a region code or US state name, keep only the rows whose AIRPORT_REGION equals that region; rows without region data (other countries, web rows) are dropped by a region filter.
  4. Same-country, far-apart matches: if the remaining rows span more than one region (by AIRPORT_REGION) and no region was stated, the city is ambiguous → None. ("Portland" → None; "Portland, OR" → PDX; "Portland, Maine" → PWM; "Portland, ME" → PWM.) Rows from countries without region data keep today's behaviour (London still → LHR,LGW,STN).

  5. Tests for each example above plus "Springfield, IL" when present in the seed (else skip), "Birmingham, AL" → BHM, "Birmingham, UK" → BHX, "San Jose, CA" → SJC, "Victoria, BC" → YYJ.

  6. City spelling normalisation (both lookup_city_iata and static_results.normalise_place / _place_country):

  7. One shared helper in backend/app/core/places.py: fold_place(text) -> str — NFKD + strip combining marks, plus explicit transliteration for ß→ss, ø→o, æ→ae, œ→oe, ł→l, đ→d, ı→i, þ→th, ð→d; lower-case, collapse whitespace.
  8. A small CITY_ALIASES map (folded alias → DB city spelling), at minimum: washington / washington dc / washington d c / washington d.c. / dc → "Washington D.C."; saint petersburg / st petersburg → "St. Petersburg"; new york city / nyc → "New York" (only when not a bare code — the bare-code path wins for "NYC"); saigon → "Ho Chi Minh City"; bombay → "Mumbai". Verify each target exists in the seed (test).
  9. lookup_city_iata queries city IN (:typed, :folded, :alias) with COLLATE NOCASE (still indexed, one query). "Ålesund" must still match when typed with or without the ring.
  10. _place_country: fold the city before the city-map lookup and fold the map keys once (accented keys like "são paulo" stay valid). "Zürich" / "Zurich, Switzerland" / "São Paulo, BR" / "Washington" / "Washington DC" / "Washington, D.C." all resolve (switzerland / brazil / usa). "Washington" alone must not become ambiguous with the US state name — usa either way.

  11. Tests: "São Paulo" → GRU (+ others in the seed), "Zürich" → ZRH, "Düsseldorf" → DUS, "Kraków" → KRK, "Malmö" → MMX, "Reykjavík" → RKV (+KEF if seeded as Reykjavik), "Washington" / "Washington, DC" / "Washington D.C." → IAD,DCA, "Saint Petersburg" → LED, "St Petersburg" → LED, "Ålesund"/"Alesund" → AES.

  12. Fare calendar selected-date price agrees with the cards (serp_flights.py):

  13. The main round-trip / one-way search records the cheapest outbound-stage price (_cheapest(data1) / _cheapest(data)) for its dates when it ran unfiltered, by writing the per-date calendar cache entry the calendar already reads (serp-cal: key, same format as search_calendar uses).
  14. search_calendar selected date: min(cheapest outbound-stage price for that date, cheapest mapped card price from the cached main search), either may be missing; fall back to Google's lowest_price only when both are missing. Update _cached_selected_price and its docstring accordingly; non-selected dates unchanged.
  15. Tests (mocked _call): main search writes the cal cache entry when unfiltered and not when filtered; selected date = cheapest card when the cards are cheaper than lowest_price (the $341 vs $360 case); selected date = outbound cheapest when no cards; lowest_price only when neither exists; existing calendar tests stay green.

Docs: API-Reference / Agent-System lines that describe city resolution and the fare calendar.

Goal: (1) Free-text cities ("Berlin", "Berlin, Germany", "BER — Berlin, Germany") get real airport codes for live flight search and the fare calendar. (2) "City, XX" where XX is an ISO country code resolves to that country in the reference tables. (3) The chat itinerary prompt asks for durations and coordinates like the main itinerary prompt.

Spec: Follow-ups surfaced on 2026-10-30. Choices are Claude's (user delegated).

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
1. City → airport codes (backend):
  2. Where: the TravelSearchRequest validator that today resolves 3-letter codes (backend/app/schemas/request.py resolve_iata_codes, origin_iata / destination_iata excluded fields) — extend it so that when origin/destination is NOT already a code, it looks the place up in the local airports database (the same data /api/airports/search serves; find the DB helper in backend/app/db/) by city name: first comma segment (after stripping a leading "XXX — " prefix), case-insensitive exact city match; if a country is given (last comma segment), restrict to that country (accept common names/aliases the DB uses); pick up to 3 airports in that city, primary/largest first if the DB has such a signal, else stable by code; set origin_iata/destination_iata to the comma-joined list (SerpAPI accepts comma lists for departure_id/arrival_id).
  3. Multi-city: apply the same to each destinations[] entry wherever the multi-city flight search reads codes (check serp_flights multi-city params builder).
  4. NEVER perform web/network lookups in this path (the existing web fallback for unknown 3-letter codes is untouched); unknown city → leave unset → today's behaviour (AI estimate).
  5. serp_flights._build_params (and the calendar) must use the resolved codes; verify the existing code already prefers origin_iata/destination_iata, otherwise wire it.
  6. Tests (DB seeded in tests as other tests do): "Berlin" → BER; "Berlin, Germany" → BER; "BER — Berlin, Germany" → BER; "London" → up to 3 London airports incl. LHR; "Paris, Texas" → none (no match in that country); "Springfield" ambiguity without country → pick only if all matches share one country, else none; codes passed through unchanged; _build_params uses the comma list; no network calls (monkeypatch any web helper to fail).
  7. ISO country codes in reference lookups (backend/app/agents/static_results.py _place_country / normaliser):
  8. Add an ISO-3166 alpha-2 → table-country map for every country present in the reference tables (and their aliases).
  9. Rule for a trailing ≤2-letter segment: if the city-map country for the city equals the ISO code's country → that country; else if the code is an ISO code and the city is unknown → that country; else if it's a US state code and the city-map says usa (or the city is unknown and the code is not an ISO country) → usa; otherwise no row. Examples (tests): "Berlin, DE" → germany; "Toronto, CA" → canada; "Bali, ID" → indonesia; "Delhi, IN" → india; "Miami, FL" → usa; "Paris, FR" → france; "Paris, TX" → no row; "Paris, Texas" → no row. The existing lookup regression suite must stay green.
  10. Chat itinerary prompt (backend/app/agents/chat_itinerary_agent.py): require duration_hours on every slot and lat/lng on every slot (approximate neighbourhood or hotel coordinates when there's no specific place), matching .agents/itinerary.md wording; prompt test like backend/tests/test_itinerary_timing_prompt.py.

docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: Every itinerary activity shows an estimated start–end time and the travel time from the previous stop; days that don't fit are flagged; times follow the user's drag-and-drop edits and flow into Timeline, calendar export, print, share and the Health Check re-check.

Spec: Backlog #18. Facts: research-16-18-9.md (#18 section) in the scratchpad. Choices are Claude's.

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Options weighed: (a) LLM emits times — rejected: stale as soon as the user moves an activity, and unverifiable; (b) deterministic client-side scheduler applied after arrangeItinerary — chosen: one source of truth that re-runs on every edit; positions/keys (<day>-<time_of_day>) unchanged, so edits/notes/plan picks/.ics UIDs keep working.

Scheduler (pure frontend/src/utils/schedule.js, unit-tested, node env): - scheduleDays(days, edits = {}) -> days' (new objects) adding to each slot start_time "HH:MM", end_time, transit_from_prev: { minutes, mode: 'walk'|'transit', km } | null, and to each day schedule_warnings: string[]. - Bucket anchors: morning 09:00, afternoon 13:30, evening 18:30; slots ordered by existing rank (time_of_day order, odd slots by slotRanks rule — reuse helpers from itineraryLayout.js). - Duration: duration_hours (finite, 0.25–12) else defaults morning 3h / afternoon 3h / evening 2.5h; edits don't change duration. - Transit between consecutive slots: if both have finite lat/lng → km = haversine × 1.3; walk if km ≤ 1.5 (4.5 km/h), else transit (20 km/h + 10 min); minutes rounded up to 5; first slot of a day has no transit. Missing coords → transit_from_prev: null but scheduling assumes a 20-min buffer. - start = max(anchor, prev.end + transit/buffer); end = start + duration. - Warnings: start pushed > 45 min past its anchor → " starts at 14:20 — later than planned"; day ends after 23:00 → "Day N runs past 23:00". Days with no standard slots untouched. - Shared haversine: extract haversineKm from TripMap.jsx into frontend/src/utils/geo.js (TripMap imports it).

Wiring (renderers use scheduleDays(arrangeItinerary(...).days, edits)): - ItinerarySection: row shows "09:00–12:00" under the time-of-day label; between rows a muted transit line ("🚶 12 min walk · 0.9 km" / "🚇 ~25 min by transit" / nothing when unknown); a per-day amber "Tight schedule" chip listing warnings; a one-line note "Times are estimates based on typical durations and distances." - TimelineView: show times in each slot card. - planExport.js (.ics): use start_time/end_time when present (fallback SLOT_HOURS unchanged → existing tests stay green); planItineraryDays returns scheduled days. - planPrint.js, SharePage.jsx, PlanViewModal.jsx: show "09:00–12:00" next to time_of_day. - Stress-test re-check payload (utils/stressTestPayload.js from the polish branch): include start/end/transit; backend stress_test_agent._summarize_itinerary prints HH:MM–HH:MM and transit minutes when present (backend unit test). - Prompts: .agents/itinerary.md and backend/app/agents/itinerary_agent.py — require duration_hours on every slot and lat/lng on every slot that names a specific place (no other changes); backend fallback itinerary unchanged. - ChatPage unchanged. - Docs: Frontend.md, Agent-System.md one line.
